title: Risk-adapted MRI Protocols for the Detection of Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Purpose To compare the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of three MRI protocols for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) according to prebiopsy risk. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included 390 male patients who underwent prostate multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) between January 2019 and April 2024 for suspected csPCa, followed by biopsy. Patients were stratified by Rotterdam Prostate Cancer Risk Calculator score into low-risk (<4%), intermediate-risk (4%-9%), and high-risk (≥10%) groups. Three datasets were generated from each examination: mpMRI (T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging [DWI], and dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging), unenhanced MRI (multiplanar T2-weighted imaging and DWI), and short MRI (axial T2-weighted imaging and DWI). Overall, 1170 datasets were randomly assigned to 10 expert radiologists (117 examinations each). Diagnostic performance for grade group 2 or greater cancer and clinical utility metrics were compared across risk groups. Results Among the 390 patients (median age, 66 years [IQR, 61-71 years]), csPCa prevalence was 34.4% (134 of 390). In low-risk patients, short MRI demonstrated the highest sensitivity (95% [21 of 22]), with no significant differences among protocols (all P ≥ .21) and greatest potential for safe biopsy avoidance (84 biopsies avoided per missed csPCa). In intermediate-risk patients, mpMRI showed higher sensitivity (83% vs 72% for unenhanced MRI and 62% for short MRI; P = .012 for mpMRI vs short MRI) and higher biopsy efficiency (1.11 vs 0.85 for mpMRI vs unenhanced MRI). In high-risk patients, protocol-related differences were minimal (all P ≥ .12). Conclusion mpMRI was associated with improved sensitivity and biopsy efficiency in intermediate-risk patients, whereas protocol differences were limited in low- and high-risk groups; these findings support risk-adapted selection of MRI protocols. Keywords: MR-Dynamic Contrast-enhanced, MR Imaging, Urinary, Prostate, Neoplasms-Primary, Efficacy Studies, Prostatic Neoplasms, MRI, Contrast Medium, Biopsy, Risk Assessment Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

title: Causes of False-Negative Screening Digital Breast Tomosynthesis Examinations: A Multireader Study.
abstract: Purpose To classify the causes and pathologic characteristics of false-negative screening digital breast tomosynthesis examinations. Materials and Methods All false-negative screening examinations at a single center from March 1, 2019, through December 31, 2023, were collected. Seven fellowship-trained breast radiologists independently reviewed the false-negative screening and diagnostic mammograms preceding biopsy. For each mammogram, radiologists recorded the cancer as visible or not visible. Cancers were classified as mammographically occult (not visible on mammogram), missed (visible on screening mammogram), or true interval cancers (visible on diagnostic mammogram only). Between-classification comparisons were performed with the Pearson χ 2 test or analysis of variance. Results A total of 117 female patients (median age, 60 years [IQR, 49-70 years]) with false-negative screening mammograms were included. Most cancers manifested symptomatically (88 of 117, 75.2%) a median of 237 days (IQR, 187-301 days) after screening mammography. Among cancers, 47.9% (56 of 117), 26.5% (31 of 117), and 25.6% (30 of 117) were missed, mammographically occult, and true interval cancers, respectively. True interval cancers were more often estrogen receptor- (50.0% [15 of 30] vs 16.1% [five of 31] vs 21.8% [12 of 55]) and progesterone receptor-negative (66.7% [20 of 30] vs 22.6% [seven of 31] vs 35.7% [20 of 56]) than mammographically occult and missed cancers. Mammographically occult cancers were more often stage T0 (32.3% [10 of 31] vs 7.1% [four of 56] vs 10.0% [three of 30]) and detected at MRI (48.4% [15 of 31] vs 3.6% [two of 56] vs 10.0% [three of 30]) and developed in younger female patients (51 vs 62 vs 59 years of age, all P < .05) than missed and true interval cancers. Conclusion Half of false-negative screening mammograms were missed, one-quarter were true interval, and one-quarter were mammographically occult cancer, with differences in pathologic characteristics. Keywords: Mammography, Screening © RSNA, 2026 See also the commentary by Elahi and Slanetz in this issue.

title: Robotic Flexible Ureteroscopy: A Step-by-Step Guide to the ILY® Platform.
abstract: Introduction Robotic flexible ureteroscopy (rfURS) is emerging as an alternative to manual flexible ureteroscopy for the treatment of upper urinary tract stones. Contemporary guidelines and reviews describe its potential ergonomic and radiation-related advantages, as well as comparable surgical outcomes (1-5). Initial clinical and simulation studies with the ILY® platform have demonstrated feasibility, safety, and a short learning curve, although standardized implementation remains limited (6-10). This video presents a step-by-step workflow for the safe and efficient use of the ILY® platform. Materials and methods A 43-year-old woman with a previous right double-J stent placed for obstructive pyelonephritis underwent rfURS for a 13-mm renal pelvic stone (1,497 HU; volume 1,214 mm³). The video demonstrates operating-room setup, robot calibration and sterile draping, robot positioning and fixation, docking to the ureteral access sheath and ureteroscope assembly, console-controlled navigation, laser lithotripsy, systematic renal inspection, and standardized undocking. A flexible suction sheath was used throughout the procedure. Results Draping and docking times were 167 and 645 seconds, respectively. Robotic console time was 115 minutes, including 52 minutes of laser lithotripsy at 8 Hz and 1.2 J. Basket extraction was not required. Undocking was completed in 74 seconds, and total operative time was 130 minutes. No intraoperative complications or troubleshooting events occurred. Postoperative day-1 computed tomography confirmed stone-free status. The patient was discharged at 36 hours postoperatively without complications, as graded by the Clavien-Dindo classification (11). Surgeon satisfaction was rated 8 out of 10. Conclusion rfURS using the ILY® platform was feasible, safe, and effective. A standardized step-by-step workflow may facilitate adoption, improve procedural consistency, and enhance surgeon ergonomics (12). rfURS represents a meaningful step toward autonomous surgery (13).

title: Outcome of Children Treated with Rituximab for Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome: Renal Histopathology as a Response Marker.
abstract: Background Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) in children remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) are commonly used as first-line therapy, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve remission, and prolonged use may result in nephrotoxicity. Rituximab has emerged as a potential therapeutic option for refractory SRNS; however, treatment responses appear variable, and the influence of underlying renal histopathology remains incompletely understood. Objectives To evaluate the association between renal histopathological findings and clinical response to rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS). Methods Study Design and Setting:This prospective observational study was conducted between 2011 and 2020 at a university-affiliated tertiary pediatric nephrology center. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) and to examine the association between renal histopathological findings and treatment response. Twenty-four children aged 2-12 years were enrolled.Follow-up:Patients were followed prospectively after completion of rituximab therapy through regular clinical and laboratory assessments. The mean follow-up duration after the last rituximab infusion was 5.1 years (range: 6 months-8 years).Treatment Response Definitions:Complete remission was defined according to International Pediatric Nephrology Association (IPNA) recommendations as a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) ≤20 mg/mmol (≤0.2 mg/mg) or negative/trace proteinuria on dipstick testing on at least three consecutive occasions.Partial remission was defined as a UPCR >20 mg/mmol but <200 mg/mmol together with serum albumin ≥30 g/L.No response was defined as failure to achieve either complete or partial remission.Genetic Evaluation:Genetic testing was performed in all patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), classic minimal change disease (MCD), and MCD with IgM deposition. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants associated with monogenic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome were identified in the tested patients. Genetic testing was not performed in patients with IgA nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, C1q nephropathy, or dense deposit disease. Results Twenty-four children with SRNS were included (13 males and 11 females; age range 2-12 years). Histopathological diagnoses included focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) in 9 patients (37.5%), minimal change disease (MCD) in 4 (16.7%), MCD with IgM deposition in 6 (25.0%), dense deposit disease in 2 (8.3%), membranous nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), IgA nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), and C1q nephropathy in 1 (4.2%). Overall, 10 patients (41.7%) achieved complete remission and 3 (12.5%) achieved partial remission, predominantly among patients with MCD and MCD with IgM deposition. Responses were uncommon among patients with FSGS. Eleven patients (45.8%), all of whom were non-responders, progressed to end-stage kidney disease. No major adverse effects of rituximab were observed; mild infusion reactions occurred in three patients and mild cellulitis in one patient. Conclusion In this cohort of children with refractory SRNS, favorable responses to rituximab were observed predominantly among patients with CNI- resistant MCD and MCD with IgM deposition, whereas responses among patients with FSGS were uncommon. These findings suggest that renal histopathology may help identify patients more likely to benefit from rituximab therapy; however, the small sample size, heterogeneous histopathological distribution, and observational study design preclude definitive conclusions. Larger prospective multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive genetic evaluation are required to determine whether histopathology can serve as a reliable predictor of rituximab responsiveness.

title: Proximal Scaphoid Pole Reconstruction Utilizing Ipsilateral Proximal Hamate Autograft.
abstract: Proximal pole scaphoid fractures complicated by nonunion and osteonecrosis present a challenging scenario with few good reconstructive options, especially when the proximal fragment is small or fragmented1-4. The use of an ipsilateral proximal hamate osteochondral autograft has emerged as a promising technique for reconstructing the proximal scaphoid pole, with the potential to restore carpal mechanics while avoiding the morbidity associated with free vascularized bone grafts or distant autograft sites. The procedure involves replacing the diseased proximal scaphoid with a structurally matched osteochondral graft from the ipsilateral proximal hamate. After excising the necrotic or fragmented scaphoid pole, a size-matched graft-harvested with its attached volar capitohamate ligament-is rotated 180° on its longitudinal axis to replicate normal scaphoid anatomy. The defect is measured in 3 planes using the scapholunate joint (proximal) and viable distal scaphoid surface as boundaries. On the hamate, an osteotomy is marked 8 to 10 mm distal to its proximal tip, parallel to the articular surface. The volar capitohamate ligament is preserved to guide graft orientation and maintain stability. These measurements align with recent anatomic and biomechanical studies that have confirmed 6 to 10-mm grafts accurately reproduce scaphoid morphology without compromising carpal kinematics. The graft is then inserted into the defect and secured with rigid internal fixation (headless compression screws or Kirschner wires). Residual gaps may be filled with cancellous bone graft. Scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) reconstruction is typically performed by suturing the hamate's volar capitohamate ligament to the dorsal SLIL remnant on the lunate with a 2-0 nonabsorbable suture. In patients with a partially intact SLIL, such as after failed fixation, the hamate graft alone may provide adequate stability, making formal reconstruction unnecessary. If intraoperative findings reveal dorsal scapholunate instability or an attenuated SLIL, reconstruction is indicated. Healthy, tensionable ligament remnants are repaired directly or reinforced with suture anchors. When dorsal fibers are deficient but volar remnants remain, the attached volar capitohamate ligament is used for reinforcement. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient begins a structured hand therapy program. Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts (e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis1,2. These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal restoration of wrist biomechanics. The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting to salvage procedures. Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the level of the contralateral wrist. Complications are rare but include nonunion, donor-site pain, and persistent stiffness. title: All-Suture Fixation for Acute Turf Toe Injuries.
abstract: Turf toe is a hallux metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) injury caused by hyperextension of the great toe with axial loading1,2. High-grade injuries may threaten return to sport and require surgery3,4. Here, we describe a capsular reconstruction of the great toe MTPJ with all-knotless suture anchors and suture tape augmentation for turf toe injuries, in isolation or in combination with a traumatic bunion, designed to reduce suture burden, minimize soft-tissue irritation, and facilitate recovery. The procedure begins with the patient supine. A direct medial approach to the hallux MTPJ is performed. Both the medial base of the proximal phalanx and the medial eminence of the metatarsal head are drilled at isometric points, and augmentation with suture tape is then performed. Isometric drill holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for suture tape augmentation. A knotless suture anchor is placed approximately 3 mm proximal to the articular margin of the metatarsal head, repairing the medial capsule in a horizontal mattress fashion. An additional knotless anchor is placed at the plantar plate insertion, and the suture is passed through the tibial sesamoid sling and tensioned with the toe in 20° of plantar flexion. Suture tape is secured into the proximal phalanx with an interference screw, then passed through the deep capsule into the metatarsal head, followed by the placement of an additional interference screw into the metatarsal head. The anchor is inserted into the plantar-medial proximal phalanx at the flexor hallucis brevis insertion. The toe is flexed during tensioning, then adjusted per clinical examination and the sesamoid location beneath the metatarsal head. Knotless fixation permits incremental tensioning with intraoperative assessment of motion. Final tensioning is performed with the toe in neutral to correct deformity without overconstraint, preserving range of motion. Nonoperative alternatives include rest, ice, compression and elevation; anti-inflammatory drugs; activity modification; and brief immobilization5,6. Operative alternatives include primary capsuloligamentous complex repair with nonabsorbable sutures, plantar plate advancement with bone tunnels or suture anchors if primary repair is not feasible, and concomitant procedures such as sesamoidectomy and bunionectomy based on the injury pattern2,7,8. This technique is intended for high-grade turf toe injuries with capsuloligamentous disruption, sesamoid complex insufficiency, and MTPJ instability. Nonoperative treatment may be appropriate in cases of low-grade injury; however, persistent pain, instability, or loss of push-off strength following nonoperative treatment would indicate a higher-grade injury. Compared with isolated repair or plantar plate advancement alone, this technique restores both static and dynamic stabilizers of the hallux MTPJ while addressing associated angular deformity. Suture tape augmentation resists recurrent hyperextension and valgus forces while allowing controlled physiologic motion. Knotless, low-profile suture anchors minimize bulk and hardware prominence in a region with limited soft-tissue coverage and bone stock. This construct offers a robust reconstruction option for athletes requiring predictable restoration of stability and reliable return to sport. Operative treatment of high-grade turf toe injuries has been shown to result in reliable pain relief, restored stability, and high rates of return to sport8. Previous studies have suggested improved function and earlier return to play compared with prolonged nonoperative treatment in appropriate patients6,7. Knotless suture anchors reduce implant prominence and eliminate knot-related irritation, while the small insertional diameter of the suture anchors preserves bone stock in the metatarsal head and proximal phalanx. This construct provides immediate stability while allowing controlled motion, facilitating rehabilitation, and reducing postoperative stiffness. Athletes typically return to unrestricted activity within 6 to 9 months, aided by the suture tape augmentation allowing earlier movement through the range of motion. This augmentation reduces the need for long-term spica splinting and bracing and reduces the risk of recurrence. Isometric drill holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for suture tape augmentation. title: Impact of Triple Assessment on Surgical Decision-making in Thyroid Nodule Management.
abstract: Accurate preoperative assessment of thyroid nodules is crucial for distinguishing malignant from benign lesions and making optimal decisions. Triple assessment using clinical examination, ultrasonography (USG), and fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) has been increasingly used to improve diagnostic accuracy. The aim of the study was to evaluate the efficacy of triple assessment in the detection and treatment of thyroid nodules by correlating ultrasonographic findings, clinical evaluation, and FNAC results with histopathological diagnosis. This study was a prospective observational study of 56 patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgical management. Data were collected prospectively using structured case record forms. Baseline information, physical examination findings, USG features, FNAC records, operative details, and histopathological reports were documented. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Frequency and percentage were used to present categorical variables. The diagnostic accuracy of clinical examination, USG, FNAC, and triple assessment was evaluated by estimating specificity, sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value, and diagnostic accuracy. A higher proportion of participants were female (85.7%) and were in the 41-60 years old age group. Histopathology confirmed benign lesions in 57.14% and malignant lesions in 42.86% of cases. Triple assessment achieved the most effective diagnostic accuracy, showing a sensitivity of 100%, a specificity of 87.50%, with a NPV of 100% and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 97.86%. Triple assessment is a dependable and useful modality for assessing thyroid nodules. Combined use of clinical examination, USG, and FNAC reduces false-negative results and supports appropriate clinical decision-making.

title: Evaluating the Interplay and Impact of Quality and Technical Variations on Performance of AI Models in Multi-Institutional Prostate MRI Datasets
abstract: Purpose: To evaluate whether visually assessed high-quality prostate MRI, as defined by the Prostate Imaging Quality (PI-QUAL) scoring system, is sufficient to ensure consistent AI model performance, or whether hidden acquisition-related technical effects introduce variability that cannot be detected through visual inspection. Methods: This retrospective study included 568 bpMRI scans from seven institutions, classified using PI-QUAL v2 into high-quality (scores 2-3) and low-quality (score 1) groups. Quantitative image quality features were extracted using MRQy from T2w and ADC sequences. Three experiments were conducted on high-quality scans: (1) unsupervised clustering to identify hidden technical batch effects; (2) V-Net models (M) for prostate capsule segmentation on T2w using single-cluster and balanced multi-cluster training strategies; and (3) VoxelMorph-based deformable registration (M2) to align ADC maps to T2w images. Performance metrics included DSC, precision, recall, volume ratio, HD95, ASSD, and TRE. Kruskal-Wallis tests assessed cross-cluster variability, Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) evaluated performance equivalence, and bootstrap resampling quantified training efficiency. Results: Clustering identified four clusters among 277 high-quality bpMRI scans. Single-cluster models showed variable performance (DSC=0.41-0.85) with significant batch effects (p<0.001), even with 140 training samples. The balanced multi-cluster model (n=60) eliminated batch effects (p=0.075), achieved equivalent performance (p<0.001), and demonstrated 2.23-fold greater training efficiency despite using 2.3-fold fewer samples. Registration performance also varied significantly across clusters (TRE=0.86-5.47 mm, p<0.001). Conclusion: Acquisition-related batch effects significantly impact AI generalizability in prostate MRI, even among high-quality scans. Quantitative clustering enables detection of technical variations and supports diversity-aware training strategies that achieve equivalent performance with 2.3-fold fewer samples while eliminating batch effects.

title: Vascular Proximity Coverage: A Novel CT-Based Marker of Pulmonary Vascular Distance to the Lung Parenchyma
abstract: Rationale: Conventional CT-derived pulmonary vascular metrics quantify vascular pruning but do not assess the spatial heterogeneity of vascular architecture. In COPD, peripheral microvascular pruning coexists with compensatory central vessel dilation, paradoxically preserving total vessel volume while reducing effective vascular penetration into lung parenchyma. Objectives: To develop and evaluate Vascular Proximity Coverage (VPC), a distance-based CT biomarker quantifying the spatial efficiency of pulmonary vascular distribution. Methods: This retrospective analysis included 7,881 COPDGene participants [PHASE] with complete vascular segmentations. VPC was estimated by integrating the area under the cumulative lung tissue coverage curve at distances of 0-10 mm from segmented vessel voxels. Multivariable models assessed associations with lung function, six-minute walk distance (6MWD), St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) score, mMRC dyspnea score, and all-cause mortality over a median follow-up of [10.8] years, adjusting for demographics, smoking, emphysema, scanner type, and BV5. The cohort was stratified at median BV5 and VPC into concordant (high/high, low/low) and discordant (high-BV5/low-VPC, low-BV5/high-VPC) vascular phenotypes. Results: VPC declined across disease severity (5.82 {+/-} 0.50 [UNITS] in non-smokers to 5.21 {+/-} 0.64 in GOLD 4; p < 0.001). Among spirometrically normal smokers, current smokers had lower VPC than former smokers (5.31 vs. 5.68; p < 0.001). Each standard deviation decrease in VPC was independently associated with reduced 6MWD ({beta} = -16.8 m, 95% CI: -19.5 to -14.0), worse SGRQ ({beta} = 1.9, 95% CI: 1.4 to 2.4), and greater dyspnea (RR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.08; all p < 0.001). The lowest VPC quartile was associated with 38% higher mortality than the reference quartile (HR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.18 to 1.62; p < 0.001). The high-BV5/low-VPC phenotype showed 24% higher mortality than high-BV5/high-VPC (HR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.08 to 1.42; p = 0.002) despite preserved vessel volume. Conclusions: VPC captures spatial heterogeneity of vascular architecture independent of vessel volume, is reduced in smokers without airflow obstruction, and identifies excess mortality risk among individuals whose total vessel volume appears preserved.

title: Deep Learning-Based Anatomical Level Classification of Craniofacial CT Slices: Comparison of CNN Architectures and Ensemble Methods
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) interpretation requires recognition of the anatomical level of each slice. Classification may facilitate preprocessing and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. We developed deep learning models to classify craniofacial CT slices into six anatomical categories. A total of 11,769 images were collected from a multicenter database involving 10 Japanese university hospitals and the public Head-Neck-Radiomics-HN1 dataset. Patients were divided into training (70%) and evaluation (30%) sets. Five CNN architectures were trained from scratch, and hard- and soft-voting ensembles were evaluated. Individual-model accuracy ranged from 94.72% to 96.09%; the hard-voting ensemble achieved 96.46% accuracy (Cohen's k = 0.954). Although performance differed among individual models (Cochran's Q = 99.29, p < 0.001), the ensemble did not significantly outperform EfficientNetV2B1 (McNemar's p = 0.163). Errors occurred mainly between adjacent anatomical regions. Deep learning can classify craniofacial CT slices accurately and may support automated dataset organization and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. External validation is needed.

title: Neurochemical fingerprinting of the Alzheimers disease continuum using 7 T short-echo-time brain single voxel 1H-MRS.
abstract: Introduction: This study aimed to characterize the neurochemical profile of Alzheimer s disease (AD) continuum stages using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) data for brain metabolites and macromolecules. We used Orthogonal Projection to Latent Structures Discriminant Analysis (OPLS-DA) to classify diagnostic groups and assess feature importance. Methods: Our dataset consisted of 7 T short-echo time 1H-MRS spectra of the posterior cingulate cortex/precuneus of individuals diagnosed with AD (n = 27) or Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI, n = 27) and Healthy Controls (HC, n = 31). Classification used 100-round Monte Carlo cross-validation based on metabolite concentrations and macromolecular peak intensities. Variable importance in projection (VIP) was assessed across classification models to identify the most relevant neurochemical features. The resulting metabolite rankings were compared with previous literature to evaluate their biological plausibility. Results: Classification was strongest for AD versus HC (AUC=0.88) and lower for comparisons involving MCI. Metabolites contributing most strongly to classification included myo-inositol, ascorbate, and choline-containing compounds, consistent with previous studies on AD-related neurochemical alterations. In addition, specific macromolecular components were identified as relevant features, suggesting a potential contribution of MM signals to the characterization of AD-related neurochemistry. Discussion: These findings support the use of short-echo-time 1H-MRS as a complementary tool for characterizing neurochemical changes in the AD continuum, with potential applications in disease characterization and monitoring, warranting validation in larger cohorts.

title: Clinical referral text overrides MRI evidence in multimodal large language models: glioma versus brain abscess
abstract: Objectives: To determine how strongly clinical referral text, rather than image content, drives the decisions of multimodal large language models (LLMs) differentiating glioma from brain abscess on MRI. Materials and methods: This retrospective single-center study included 60 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted brain MRI examinations (30 gliomas, 30 abscesses; reference-standard diagnosis). One axial slice per case was paired with five referral texts (explicitly inflammatory to explicitly tumor-suggestive) under three prompt instructions and submitted 20 times each to GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Qwen 3.6 (72,000 answers). The primary outcome was the text-driven span (difference in tumor-call frequency between explicit inflammatory and explicit tumor text). Two blinded radiologists classified the images without text; sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were compared descriptively. Results: Patients (29 women) had a mean age of 55.8 +/- 16.4 years. With neutral text, models answered tumor in 45-67% of queries (specificity, 0.38-0.78), versus 52% and 60% for radiologists (specificity, 0.77 and 0.63). The text-driven span was 0.79-1.00 (p < 0.001 for all models), whereas confirmed gliomas and abscesses differed by only 0.01-0.10 in three models and 0.25 in Gemini 3.5 Flash. Subtle wording produced at least 83% of the span in three models. An instruction to ignore the text reduced the span to 0.48-0.70 in three models and to 0.04 in Gemini 3.5 Flash, partly through reversion to a tumor default. Model accuracy was 0.52-0.73 versus 0.78 and 0.73 for radiologists. Conclusion: Multimodal LLMs deferred to referral text over imaging evidence in differentiating glioma from brain abscess, and prompt instructions did not reliably correct this.

title: Foundation Model-Enabled Pathology-Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

title: Morphometric analysis and three-dimensional reconstruction of sphenoid sinus: associations of linear dimensions and volume with pneumatization patterns and neurovascular relationships.
abstract: The sphenoid sinus (SS) shows morphological variability relevant to endoscopic endonasal skull-base access. This study examined associations of SS volume and linear dimensions with pneumatization patterns, extensions, and neurovascular anatomy. This retrospective study included 253 adult sinus computed tomography (CT) examinations. Μaximum anteroposterior (AP max), laterolateral (LL max), and craniocaudal (CC max) dimensions were measured, and SS volume was calculated by semi-automated three-dimensional contouring with manual refinement. Pneumatization patterns and relationships with the internal carotid artery (ICA), optic nerve (ON), and Vidian nerve (VN) were examined using exploratory univariable logistic regression, supplemented by separate age- and sex-adjusted models for neurovascular outcomes. Mean SS volume was 11.12 ± 4.50cm³. Males had greater volume (p = 0.001) and AP max (p = 0.013) than females. Volume correlated strongly with LL max (r = 0.791) and AP max (r = 0.705) (both p < 0.001). Each 1-mm increase in AP max was associated with posterior extension (OR = 1.57, 95% CI 1.40-1.76) and ICA (OR = 1.22), ON (OR = 1.13), and VN (OR = 1.24) protrusion and/or dehiscence. Each 1-mm increase in LL max was associated with lateral extension (OR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.28-1.52) and VN protrusion and/or dehiscence (OR = 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.31) (p < 0.001). Greater SS volume was associated with protrusion and/or dehiscence of all three structures, and remained associated with these neurovascular outcomes after adjustment for age and sex. SS volume and linear dimensions provide complementary quantitative information on the magnitude and direction of pneumatization. AP max and LL max were associated with specific extension patterns and with neurovascular protrusion and/or dehiscence.

title: Clinical phenotype and bone microarchitecture of cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome: experience from a single center in China.
abstract: Cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome (CSHS) is a rare mosaic RASopathy characterized by epidermal or melanocytic nevi, skeletal dysplasia, and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)-mediated hypophosphatemic rickets. However, its bone microarchitectural features remain underdefined. The study aimed to characterize the clinical, genetic, and skeletal microarchitectural features of CSHS. We summarized clinical findings of 6 CSHS patients with genetically confirmed somatic RAS mutations. Skeletal involvement was assessed by whole-body bone scintigraphy. High-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography parameters at the distal radius and tibia were compared with age- and sex-matched XLH controls (1:3). Literature review of 24 genetically confirmed CSHS patients was performed to assess genotype-phenotype correlation. All patients were confirmed to carry somatic HRAS or NRAS mutation in affected skin. Hypophosphatemia, elevated alkaline phosphatase and elevated FGF23 were found in all patients. Genotype-phenotype correlation analysis did not identify any significant biochemical or systemic burden differences across 3 genotypes. Compared with XLH controls, CSHS patients exhibited significantly reduced total and trabecular volumetric BMD (vBMD), with relatively preserved cortical vBMD. Bone cross-sectional geometry was less expanded than in XLH at the tibia. In addition, thinner trabeculae with greater separation were found at the radius, and the distal tibia showed thinner cortices and decreased cortical porosity. Estimated bone stiffness and failure load were significantly lower at both the radius and tibia. CSHS is associated with pronounced trabecular vBMD impairment and reduced bone strength compared with XLH controls. These findings are consistent with a combined contribution of intrinsic skeletal dysplasia and chronic hypophosphatemia on bone, although further studies are needed to elucidate these mechanisms.

title: Preliminary study on early microvascular ingrowth into distracted callus during distraction osteogenesis-A non-invasive approach to explore the early growth patterns and possible mechanism of distraction osteogenesis in vivo.
abstract: Distraction osteogenesis (DO) is critical for repairing large segmental bone defects. Early callus vascularization is essential for bone regeneration; however, real-time microcirculatory assessment remains lacking. This study aimed to elucidate spatiotemporal microvascular network construction in distracted callus using super-resolution contrast-enhanced ultrasound (SR CEUS) and high-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (HiFR CEUS) in a sheep tibial DO model. Six sheep underwent tibial DO. On day 7 of distraction, B-mode ultrasound, "Firefly" imaging, SR CEUS, and HiFR CEUS were performed. Quantitative parameters including vessel density (VD), perfusion index (PI), mean intensity, and peak intensity (PKI) were compared among three regions: central high-perfusion area (CHPA), annular low-perfusion area (ALPA), and peripheral high-perfusion area (PHPA). B-mode ultrasound revealed outward bulging of distracted callus. "Firefly" imaging detected microcalcifications. SR CEUS showed PHPA (67.58% of cross-sectional area) received centripetal blood flow from periosteum and surrounding soft tissues; CHPA (10.39%) received centrifugal flow from the medullary cavity; ALPA (22.03%), located between them, exhibited significantly lower mean intensity than CHPA/PHPA and significantly lower VD and PI than PHPA (P < 0.05). HiFR CEUS showed perfusion appeared first in CHPA, then PHPA, and lastly ALPA. SR and HiFR CEUS enable non-invasive, dynamic visualization and quantification of microvascular growth in distracted callus, revealing a "target ring sign", "bidirectional fusion" perfusion pattern, and "central-first, peripheral-second" perfusion sequence. ALPA was identified as a hypovascular zone potentially associated with delayed mineralization or cyst formation. This system provides a novel imaging framework for early assessment of callus viability, prediction of osteogenic risk, and guidance of individualized distraction strategies.

B-mode ultrasound revealed outward bulging of distracted callus. "Firefly" imaging detected microcalcifications. SR CEUS showed PHPA (67.58% of cross-sectional area) received centripetal blood flow from periosteum and surrounding soft tissues; CHPA (10.39%) received centrifugal flow from the medullary cavity; ALPA (22.03%), located between them, exhibited significantly lower mean intensity than CHPA/PHPA and significantly lower VD and PI than PHPA (P < 0.05). HiFR CEUS showed perfusion appeared first in CHPA, then PHPA, and lastly ALPA. SR and HiFR CEUS enable non-invasive, dynamic visualization and quantification of microvascular growth in distracted callus, revealing a "target ring sign", "bidirectional fusion" perfusion pattern, and "central-first, peripheral-second" perfusion sequence. ALPA was identified as a hypovascular zone potentially associated with delayed mineralization or cyst formation. This system provides a novel imaging framework for early assessment of callus viability, prediction of osteogenic risk, and guidance of individualized distraction strategies.

title: Multi-center study of CMR versus cardiac catheterization with endomyocardial biopsy for pediatric transplant surveillance: study protocol.
abstract: Notwithstanding advances in post-transplant care, acute allograft rejection (AR) remains the leading cause of mortality in pediatric heart transplant recipients (PHTX). Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) continues to be the standard of care for AR detection, despite being invasive, costly, and associated with patient discomfort and potential complications. Non-invasive alternatives, including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) with T1 and T2 parametric mapping and blood biomarkers (BB) such as cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and microRNA (miRNA), have shown promise in the adult transplant population, but their validation in the pediatric transplant population is lacking. The "Predictive Modeling of Acute Rejection in Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients" (PEACE) study is a prospective, multicenter trial aiming to assess the diagnostic accuracy of CMR and BB in comparison to EMB. The goal of this manuscript is to describe the purpose and experimental protocol of the PEACE study. The PEACE study's overarching hypothesis is that CMR and BB can consistently and accurately detect myocardial abnormalities, potentially guiding the need for EMB. Secondary objectives include cost-analyses of CMR and BB, as well as a biomarker performance evaluation in biopsy-negative, but symptomatic and suspected AR cases. PEACE will enroll PHTX ages 6-25 years, across approximately 20 U.S. pediatric hospitals. All subjects will undergo EMB for surveillance or suspected AR as standard of care. As part of the research protocol, subjects will undergo blood collection for BB prior to the EMB and CMR within 5 days of EMB. Central core labs will conduct blinded analysis for imaging, pathology, and biomarkers to ensure consistent data interpretation. PEACE represents a critical step in reducing reliance on invasive biopsies in the clinical care of PHTX. By validating non-invasive tools in a large, diverse population, the PEACE study could transform AR detection, resulting in improvement of the patient experience and outcomes in this vulnerable population. (Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07770659, Non-invasive Prediction of EArly Cardiac rEjection (PEACE)).

title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 7.0 T dental test dataset (2 subjects), our method achieved a PSNR of 27.31 [26.83, 27.79] dB and the lowest LPIPS of 0.19 [0.18, 0.20]. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.

title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

title: The PENIMA project: artificial intelligence decision-support tool for penile lesions - protocol paper and invitation to participate.
abstract: To present and describe the design, data collection framework, and interim cohort characteristics of the PENIMA project, a multicentre initiative establishing a clinically annotated penile lesion image repository to support future artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision-support development - and to encourage urology and dermatology colleagues working with penile lesions to participate in the project. Prospective participant inclusion commenced in March 2023 across Scandinavian urological and dermatological departments. Patients with penile anatomy undergoing clinically indicated genital examination are invited to participate and provide oral and written consent as defined by local authority regulations. Clinical photographs and structured metadata are collected. Lesion classification is based on a specialist evaluation, clinical follow-up and histopathology when available. Images are pseudonymised and annotated using a secure, containerised Computer Vision Annotation Tool (CVAT) environment. Supervised machine-learning model development using convolutional neural networks is planned with patient-level dataset partitioning and evaluation using standard diagnostic performance metrics. The study was approved by relevant local authorities, and the approval number is 1-10-72-150-22. As of February 2026, 1125 participants and approximately 7000 images have been included. In all, 40% represented normal anatomical variants. Among lesional cases, 33% are clinically assessed as benign, 13% premalignant, and 8% malignant; 22% of all cases have histopathological verification. Concordance between clinical suspicion and histopathology is highest for penile carcinoma (84.6%, 95% confidence interval 75.0-91.0%). The PENIMA project includes a multicentre, clinically grounded image repository reflecting real-world penile lesion presentations. The feasible and successful infrastructure provides a foundation for future development and validation of image-based clinical decision-support tools.

title: Segment-based comparison of multiparametric MRI, Gallium-68-PSMA-PET/CT and combined imaging with histopathology in prostate cancer.
abstract: To compare the segment-based diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), Gallium-68-prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (68Ga-PSMA-PET/CT), for detecting histopathologically confirmed prostate cancer (PCa). This analysis included 97 men from the prospective, interventional, phase II DEPROMP (DEtection rate of clinically significant PROstate cancer by mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT fusion biopsy) trial who underwent radical prostatectomy with whole-mount histopathological evaluation. All participants received mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT prior to biopsy. The mpMRI was interpreted according to Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version(v)2.1, and PSMA-PET/CT according to Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardised Evaluation (PROMISE) molecular imaging Tumour-Node-Metastasis (miTNM) criteria. The prostate was divided into 36 anatomical segments based on the PI-RADS v2.1 sector map. Each segment was correlated with histopathological findings from prostatectomy specimens. For each imaging modality, detection rates, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated at the segment level. A total of 3492 prostate segments were analysed. Detection rates were 74.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 72.6-75.5) for mpMRI, 72.2% (95% CI 70.6-73.6) for PSMA-PET/CT, and 79.1% (95% CI 77.7-80.4) for the combined use of mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT. Sensitivity and specificity were 13.4% and 97.3% for mpMRI, 18.5% and 92.7% for PSMA-PET/CT, and 25.8% and 90.5% for combined mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT, respectively. Threshold-based receiver operating characteristic analyses yielded an AUC of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54-0.69) for PI-RADS, 0.68 (95% CI 0.63-0.74) for maximum standardised uptake value, and 0.69 (95% CI 0.65-0.74) for molecular imaging PSMA. At the segment level, mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT showed comparable diagnostic accuracy with high specificity but limited sensitivity. Their combination improved sensitivity and overall detection performance, underscoring the complementary value of structural and molecular imaging for lesion localisation and precision management in PCa.

title: Transient apnoea for motion control during flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy: a randomised trial.
abstract: To determine whether transient apnoea (TA) during flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy improves active lithotripsy efficiency compared with regular mechanical ventilation (RMV) and small tidal-volume ventilation (STVV). In this single-centre, three-arm randomised trial, 150 adults with a single computed tomography (CT)-confirmed renal, ureteropelvic, or proximal ureteric stone measuring 10-<20 mm were assigned one-to-one-to-one to RMV, STVV, or TA. TA followed 5-min 100% oxygen pre-oxygenation, with 9-min maximum and pre-specified stopping criteria under continuous anaesthetic monitoring. The primary endpoint was active lithotripsy efficiency, defined as CT-estimated stone volume divided by elapsed active lithotripsy time. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. The mean (standard deviation) active lithotripsy efficiency was 27.8 (8.9), 26.6 (8.0), and 34.3 (10.0) mm3/min with RMV, STVV, and TA, respectively (P < 0.001). TA increased adjusted efficiency by 5.9 mm3/min vs RMV (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.2-9.6 mm3/min) and 6.8 mm3/min vs STVV (95% CI 3.3-10.2 mm3/min). The median active lithotripsy time was 27.5, 26.5, and 22.0 min (P = 0.001); total operative time was 50.0, 50.0, and 43.0 min (P = 0.002); and surgeon-rated targeting stability scores were 7.0, 7.0, and 9.0 (P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative Day 1/1-month stone-free rates were 88%/92%, 80%/96%, and 88%/90%, respectively, with no significant between-group differences. The median (interquartile range) achieved apnoea duration was 5.0 (4.5-6.8) min; 46/50 resumed ventilation before the 9-min maximum, most commonly for heart-rate decline/bradycardia (n = 27) or blood-pressure decline/hypotension (n = 20). No patient had a peripheral oxygen saturation <90% or a Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥III complication; transient hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis improved after ventilation resumed. Transient apnoea improved lithotripsy efficiency and shortened operative time compared with RMV and STVV, with higher surgeon-rated targeting stability. The benefit was primarily intraoperative, without evidence of greater postoperative stone clearance. Protocolised TA may provide a brief intraoperative motion-control option with pre-oxygenation, continuous anaesthetic monitoring, and individualised termination.

title: A Familial Case of Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre Syndrome (TROFAS), Presenting With Postaxial Polydactyly and Upper Lip Vascular Malformation.
abstract: Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre syndrome (TROFAS, OMIM #617107) is a recently identified autosomal recessive disorder characterised by syndromic overgrowth, facial dysmorphism, mild intellectual disability, variable congenital anomalies, and occasional tumour occurrence. TROFAS results from homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in the FIBP gene, encoding the intracellular binding protein for acidic fibroblast growth factor. This protein plays a role in the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling pathway, which is involved in cell proliferation and contributes to the development of several structures, such as the nervous system, optic vesicles, and blood vessels. Prior to the present report, TROFAS has been described in 10 patients from seven families, four of which are of Turkish origin. We report two additional Turkish siblings from a previously unreported family harbouring the recurrent homozygous c.412-3_415dupCAGTTTG likely pathogenic variant in FIBP. Both presented with typical TROFAS features; however, the male sibling exhibited a more severe neurodevelopmental profile and additional malformations, including postaxial polydactyly and upper lip vascular malformation, which, to our knowledge, have not previously been reported in association with TROFAS. A detailed clinical characterisation of these two new cases contributes to a more comprehensive delineation of the syndrome, adding potentially novel phenotypic features requiring confirmation in additional patients.

title: PRAME Immunohistochemistry and Molecular Profiling in Undifferentiated Cutaneous Pleomorphic Neoplasms: A Case Series of 8 Tumors.
abstract: Undifferentiated cutaneous pleomorphic neoplasms are diagnostically challenging, as histopathology and immunohistochemistry often fail to identify undifferentiated melanoma in lesions that instead remain classified provisionally as atypical fibroxanthoma (AFX) or pleomorphic dermal sarcoma (PDS). Given the prognostic and therapeutic implications of melanoma, additional ancillary tools may be helpful in selected cases. We studied eight patients with undifferentiated pleomorphic neoplasms using molecular profiling and PRAME immunohistochemistry, correlating findings with clinical behavior. Molecular findings varied across the cohort. Two tumors harbored NRAS hotspot mutations and were associated with aggressive clinical courses. In one patient, the tumor showed focal melanoma in situ associated with an undifferentiated intradermal tumor harboring NF1, TERT, and TP53 variants. The remaining tumors lacked melanoma-associated hotspot mutations. Diffuse PRAME expression was seen in three patients with an established diagnosis of melanoma and three patients with AFX/PDS. Two patients with AFX/PDS were negative for PRAME expression. Molecular profiling may provide supportive diagnostic evidence for melanoma lineage in a subset of undifferentiated cutaneous pleomorphic neoplasms when interpreted in conjunction with morphology, immunohistochemistry, and clinical findings. In contrast, diffuse PRAME expression was observed in a nonspecific fashion both in cases with melanoma driver mutations and molecularly nonspecific cases in this cohort, limiting its utility as a standalone screening test for triaging molecular analysis.

title: Ηip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure.
abstract: To determine the prevalence of neonatal hip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure and examine its association with functional level and preterm birth. We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected standardized registry data from a tertiary specialized centre providing comprehensive spina bifida diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up. Standardized hip ultrasound according to the Graf method was performed as part of a protocolized clinical pathway after prenatal surgery, within the first week of life corrected for preterm birth. The primary outcome was the prevalence of hip dysplasia at the initial ultrasound. Associations between hip status, functional level, and gestational age were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. A total of 212 children (101 males, 111 females) underwent prenatal surgical closure between 1st January 2011 and 30th August 2022; 168 children (336 hips) had available neonatal ultrasound data and were included in the analysis. Preterm birth was present in 138 (82%) of 168 children, including 99 (59%) born late preterm, 35 (21%) born very preterm, and four (2%) born extremely preterm. At the initial ultrasound, 286 (85%) of 336 hips were mature, 33 (9.8%) were immature, and 17 (5.1%) were dysplastic. Worse hip status was weakly associated with a higher functional level (r = -0.243; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was found between hip dysplasia and preterm birth (p = 0.080). The prevalence of neonatal hip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure was within the range reported for the general population.

title: Recognizing Odontogenic Maxillary Sinusitis in the ENT Clinic: Four CT Findings That Should Prompt Dental Evaluation.
abstract: Objective: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the proportion of maxillary sinuses with radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution among patients with imaging-confirmed acute or chronic maxillary sinusitis presenting to a single academic ENT clinic over one year. Sixty-five CT scans (84 sinuses) underwent multidisciplinary review for prespecified radiographic features. By highlighting imaging findings indicative of dental origin this study aims to improve recognition of possible odontogenic disease and appropriate multidisciplinary evaluation. Methods: Sixty-five patients were evaluated. Inclusion criteria required a visit diagnosis of chronic maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J32.0) or acute maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J01.00, J01.01), and a sinus CT within the preceding year. Each scan underwent multidisciplinary review by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist, an otolaryngologist, an otolaryngology resident, and a medical student. Scans were evaluated for maxillary sinus floor mucosal thickening and radiographic features suggestive of an odontogenic contribution, including periapical pathology, oroantral communication, large dental restorations, and widened periodontal ligament (PDL) space. Dental referral recommendations were based on multidisciplinary consensus from CT findings alone. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics. Results: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution were identified in 50/84 (59.52%) affected maxillary sinuses from 40 patients. Among these 50 sinuses, 17 (34%) showed widened PDL space, 15 (30%) showed oroantral communication, 28 (56%) showed periapical pathology, and 9 (18%) showed large dental restorations. There was consensus among the multidisciplinary team that in retrospect, among the 40 patients with OS, 38 required dental referrals. Conclusion: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution indicated a higher single-center cohort prevalence than expected based on population-level prevalence reports. The findings support deliberate review of the maxillary dentition on sinus CT, with this study outlining the key imaging features for odontogenic sinusitis.

title: Cardiac diagnostic modalities in polycythemia vera: A narrative review.
abstract: Polycythemia vera is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm in which erythrocytosis, Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription activation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal blood-cell activation converge to increase cardiovascular risk. This narrative review examines how electrocardiography, echocardiography, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and right-heart catheterization contribute to recognition and characterization of cardiac involvement in polycythemia vera. Reported abnormalities include QT and P-wave changes, atrial arrhythmias, acute coronary syndromes, subclinical biventricular dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, intracardiac thrombosis, and hypertrophic remodeling. Large observational datasets in myeloproliferative neoplasms also exhibit clinically important burdens of myocardial infarction, heart-failure hospitalization, bleeding, and echocardiographic pulmonary hypertension, although polycythemia vera-specific estimates remain limited. Baseline cardiovascular testing is increasingly relevant before novel therapies and trial enrollment; however, an abnormal test should prompt confirmation, reversible-cause assessment, and protocol-specific review rather than be treated as a universal contraindication. Hematocrit control and low-dose aspirin reduce thrombotic events, while evidence that cytoreductive therapy reverses electrocardiography or imaging abnormalities remains sparse. A symptom- and risk-directed diagnostic approach, integrated with hematology and cardiology assessment, is therefore more defensible than routine universal cardiac screening.

title: An Integrated Approach to MSI-High Colorectal Cancer Therapy in a Young Patient: A Clinical Case.
abstract: BACKGROUND Colorectal cancer (CRC) is extremely rare in adolescents and often presents with advanced disease because of nonspecific symptoms. Deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) and microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) are important biomarkers that influence prognosis, treatment selection, and the need for genetic evaluation. We report the case of an adolescent with MSI-H-associated CRC presenting with acute intestinal obstruction. CASE REPORT A 16-year-old male initially underwent appendectomy for presumed acute appendicitis. Persistent postoperative bowel obstruction prompted computed tomography (CT), revealing a descending colon tumor requiring emergency Hartmann's procedure. Histopathology demonstrated mucinous adenocarcinoma, pT4N0M0, with vascular invasion. Immunohistochemistry showed loss of MSH2/MSH6 expression with retained MLH1/PMS2, indicating dMMR and findings highly suggestive of Lynch syndrome, although germline testing was unavailable. Molecular analysis identified a KRAS mutation without NRAS alterations. Given his multiple high-risk features, including T4 disease, bowel obstruction, vascular invasion, mucinous histology, and very young age, he received 12 cycles of adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy. Treatment was well tolerated, and he remains disease-free more than 5 years after completion of therapy. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of adolescent CRC and the need to consider colorectal malignancy in young patients with persistent or atypical abdominal symptoms. Routine MMR/MSI testing and comprehensive molecular profiling are essential in young-onset CRC to identify patients who may have hereditary cancer syndromes and require genetic counseling. Although limited to a single case, this report underscores the importance of multidisciplinary decision-making and individualized treatment based on clinicopathological and molecular characteristics, which may contribute to favorable long-term outcomes.

title: Artificial intelligence in ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography: a bibliometric analysis.
abstract: Aim To analyze research landscapes, hotspots, and trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applied to ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) from 2015 to 2024, aiming to reveal global collaborations and guide future research. Methods We retrieved publications from Web of Science Core Collection using AI and OCTA-related search terms. After screening, 237 articles were analyzed with CiteSpace (version 6.3.R1) for co-citation, collaboration, and keyword burst analysis. Results Annual publications grew rapidly since 2017. China (94 publications) and the US (86 publications) were the most productive and influential countries. Research focused on: deep learning algorithms and vessel segmentation, ocular disease diagnosis including diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, and automated vascular quantification and multimodal imaging. Key limitations included small sample sizes and limited algorithm generalizability. Conclusion The integration of AI with OCTA has significantly advanced the automation and precise quantitative analysis of ophthalmic vascular imaging, demonstrating substantial potential for diagnosing various retinal and choroidal diseases. Future efforts should focus on developing more robust and interpretable AI models, conducting large-scale, multi-center clinical validation, and establishing standardized imaging and analysis protocols to ultimately realize the widespread adoption of AI-OCTA technology in routine clinical practice.
originalAbstract:
Aim

To analyze research landscapes, hotspots, and trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applied to ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) from 2015 to 2024, aiming to reveal global collaborations and guide future research.

Methods

We retrieved publications from Web of Science Core Collection using AI and OCTA-related search terms. After screening, 237 articles were analyzed with CiteSpace (version 6.3.R1) for co-citation, collaboration, and keyword burst analysis.

Results

Annual publications grew rapidly since 2017. China (94 publications) and the US (86 publications) were the most productive and influential countries. Research focused on: deep learning algorithms and vessel segmentation, ocular disease diagnosis including diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, and automated vascular quantification and multimodal imaging. Key limitations included small sample sizes and limited algorithm generalizability.

Conclusion

The integration of AI with OCTA has significantly advanced the automation and precise quantitative analysis of ophthalmic vascular imaging, demonstrating substantial potential for diagnosing various retinal and choroidal diseases. Future efforts should focus on developing more robust and interpretable AI models, conducting large-scale, multi-center clinical validation, and establishing standardized imaging and analysis protocols to ultimately realize the widespread adoption of AI-OCTA technology in routine clinical practice.

title: Deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognostic prediction in locally advanced cervical cancer through 18 F-FDG PET/CT and MRI combination
abstract: Abstract Background Precise pretreatment risk stratification is critical for guiding treatment intensification and personalized follow‑up in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). This study developed and validated a deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognosis prediction in patients with LACC treated with CCRT, using dual-modal pretreatment imaging from 18 F-FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI. Methods We retrospectively collected 346 patients (276 for training and 70 for testing) with LACC between June 2016 and October 2021. Radiomics and deep learning signatures were extracted from PET/CT and MRI. These signatures were integrated with the clinicopathological factors into a nomogram for clinical applications. Models were constructed using eleven machine learning algorithms, and a clinical-radiomics-deep learning model (CRDLM) was developed. The evaluation of the model’s performance was conducted through the metrics of the area under the curve (AUC). Results The CRDLM demonstrated superior predictive performance (AUCs of 0.998 (95% CI: 1.00–1.00) for training cohort and 0.901 (95% CI: 0.83–0.97) for testing cohort), which is significantly superior to conventional clinical factors (FIGO stage and SCC-Ag, AUC = 0.605–0.658). In addition, the CRDLM which combined radiomics with deep learning significantly outperformed the radiomics‑only model (AUC = 0.793, p = 0.006). Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of CRDLM reached 0.947, 0.725, and 0.786, respectively. Conclusions The CRDLM provides robust prediction of disease progression in LACC patients who received CCRT, which may facilitate personalized treatment strategies and improve clinical outcomes. Further validation in multicenter prospective studies is warranted.

title: Can Chest CT Differentiate Between Low-Risk and Higher Risk Congenital Lung Lesions in Infants?
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether chest CT can differentiate low-risk congenital lung lesions (pulmonary sequestration and CPAM type 2) from higher-risk lesions (CPAM type 1 and pleuropulmonary blastoma [PPB]) and thereby support the selection of patients for conservative management. Methods In this retrospective study (2003–2024), we identified infants with congenital lung lesions who underwent chest CT and subsequent pathologic confirmation. Two pediatric radiologists independently reviewed the anonymized CT scans, blinded to clinical and pathologic data. Lesions with a systemic arterial supply or predominant hyperinflation were classified as low risk; those with a solitary cyst, a cyst > 2 cm, or a complex cyst without systemic supply were classified as higher risk. Diagnostic confidence was graded as low, moderate, or high. Pathologic diagnosis served as the reference standard, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess interobserver agreement. title: Unintentional Weight Loss Preceding Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report and Review of Possible Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Background Unintentional weight loss is not a recognized presenting feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is more commonly associated with malignancy, chronic infection, endocrine disorders, gastrointestinal disease, or systemic inflammatory conditions. We report an unusual case in which marked involuntary weight loss preceded the diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Case Presentation: A 37-year-old man presented with acute gait impairment and right lower-extremity weakness. Retrospective history revealed gradual unintentional weight loss from approximately 97 kg to 68 kg over nearly two years despite preserved appetite and the absence of gastrointestinal, infectious, endocrine, or constitutional symptoms. Extensive investigations, including laboratory testing, infectious screening, tumor markers, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasonography, and chest imaging, failed to identify an alternative cause. Neurological examination demonstrated right lower-extremity weakness, generalized hyperreflexia, bilateral pyramidal signs, and an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 4.0. Brain and cervical spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple typical demyelinating lesions fulfilling the 2017 McDonald criteria for MS. The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by rituximab (1000 mg every 6 months). During four years of follow-up, the EDSS score improved from 4.0 to 1.0, MRI studies remained stable, and body weight gradually returned to two years before the start of the disease. Conclusion This case describes marked, unexplained weight loss preceding the diagnosis of RRMS, which resolved after treatment initiation and disease stabilization. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association suggests that clinically significant weight loss may represent an uncommon and underrecognized manifestation of active MS. Further studies are needed to clarify the frequency and mechanisms of weight changes in MS.

title: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Arising in the Aortopulmonary Window: A Case Report of Complete Resection Using Proximal Pulmonary Artery Control
abstract: Abstract Background: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is a rare malignant neoplasm, and its occurrence in the aortopulmonary window is exceptionally uncommon. Tumors in this location are technically challenging because of the limited operative space and their close relationship to the aortic arch, left pulmonary artery, left main bronchus, and left recurrent laryngeal nerve. We report a case of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma arising in the aortopulmonary window that was completely resected using a strategy for proximal pulmonary artery control. Case presentation: A 46-year-old man was referred to our institution after an abnormal mediastinal shadow was incidentally detected on chest radiography. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 48 × 29 mm well-circumscribed mass in the aortopulmonary window, broadly contacting the aorta, left pulmonary artery, and left main bronchus. Positron emission tomography showed moderate fluorodeoxyglucose uptake without distant metastasis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but did not establish a definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection was performed through median sternotomy combined with a left anterior second intercostal thoracotomy. Because direct exposure and encirclement of the tumor-adjacent left pulmonary artery were considered hazardous, proximal vascular control was established through the transverse pericardial sinus before tumor manipulation. Division of the ligamentum arteriosum increased pulmonary artery mobility and improved exposure of the operative field. The tumor was completely separated from the left pulmonary artery, aorta, left main bronchus, and recurrent laryngeal nerve without combined organ resection. Histopathological examination showed spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in whorled and rosette-like patterns. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD21, CD23, D2-40, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming follicular dendritic cell sarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 3 years after surgery. Conclusions: Complete resection of a tumor arising in the aortopulmonary window can be facilitated by secure proximal pulmonary artery control and mobilization of surrounding structures. These technical principles may also be useful for other tumors in this anatomically complex region when direct manipulation of the tumor-adjacent pulmonary artery is considered hazardous.

title: Association of intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficients with stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte levels in primary triple-negative breast cancer: a retrospective 3-T MRI study
abstract: Abstract Background Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are associated with treatment response and prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but their assessment requires tissue sampling. We investigated whether routine pretreatment imaging findings, particularly intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) measurements on 3-T breast MRI, were associated with stromal TIL levels and evaluated an exploratory MRI-based model. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 79 consecutive women with primary TNBC assessed between November 2016 and October 2023. High TIL status was defined as stromal TILs ≥ 10% in pretreatment biopsy specimens. Mammographic, ultrasonographic, MRI, and ¹⁸F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT findings were analyzed when available. A prespecified MRI-based logistic regression model included intratumoral ADC, peritumoral ADC, and MRI margin. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Associations with pathological complete response (pCR) were explored. Results High TIL status was present in 57 of 79 participants (72.2%). Among 76 participants with MRI, higher intratumoral ADC (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 6.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.47–19.67; p < 0.001) and lower peritumoral ADC (adjusted OR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.11–0.66; p = 0.004) were independently associated with high TIL status. The exploratory MRI-based model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 (95% CI, 0.879–0.989) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.914. Intratumoral ADC alone had an AUC of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.768–0.944). The associations remained consistent after adjustment for the MRI system and in the analysis restricted to the predominant Ingenia 3.0T system. In exploratory analyses, pCR was more frequent in participants with high versus low TIL status (58.1% vs. 7.7%; p = 0.001) and in those with high versus low intratumoral ADC (57.1% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.003). Conclusions Routine intratumoral and peritumoral ADC measurements were associated with high stromal TIL status in this single-center TNBC cohort. The exploratory MRI-based model showed good discrimination after bootstrap correction. External multicenter evaluation is required before clinical use.
