title: Yolo-c2ecasa: a lightweight attention-enhanced model for three-class brain tumor localization and classification in MRI.
abstract: Brain tumor localization and type classification in MRI are important tasks in computer-aided medical image analysis. However, achieving competitive localization and classification performance with lightweight models remains challenging because reducing model complexity may weaken feature representation and localization ability. In this paper, we propose YOLO-C2ECASA, a lightweight attention-enhanced object detection framework based on YOLOv11 for three-class tumor localization and classification in tumor-positive MRI images. The present study focuses on glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumors and does not address tumor-versus-no-tumor screening. The proposed C2ECASA module replaces the original self-attention design with a parameter-efficient spatial-channel attention mechanism. It integrates improved channel attention, lightweight spatial attention, C2-based feature preservation, and adaptive fusion to enhance lesion-relevant feature representation with limited computational cost. The proposed model was compared with representative object detection models. In the single-run comparison with representative object detectors, YOLO-C2ECASA maintained competitive detection performance while requiring only 2.4M parameters, 6.2G FLOPs, a model size of 5.01 MB, and a GPU inference time of 1.9 ms per image. More importantly, across ten independent runs under scratch initialization, YOLO-C2ECASA achieved mean mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 values of [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text]. Under pretrained initialization, the corresponding repeated-run results were [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text], respectively. Under CPU-only deployment, YOLO-C2ECASA achieves an inference time of 27.4 ms per image, further demonstrating its feasibility for resource-constrained environments. These results indicate that the proposed model achieves competitive detection performance while maintaining a lower computational cost than the compared detectors. Ablation and repeated-run experiments further demonstrate that the complete C2ECASA configuration achieves the highest average performance among the evaluated configurations while maintaining low computational complexity. Overall, the proposed method provides a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off for lightweight brain tumor localization and type classification in tumor-positive MRI images.

title: Ultra-High Gradient Thin-Slice Oblique Coronal Zoomed DWI for Perihilar and Distal Cholangiocarcinomas: Improved Tumor Depiction for Precise Surgical Planning.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Accurate preoperative assessment of extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (eCCA) remains challenging with conventional imaging. This study aimed to investigate the value of thin-slice oblique coronal zoomed diffusion-weighted imaging (OC-Z-DWI) on an ultra-high gradient system for eCCA (including both perihilar and distal subtypes) assessment. Materials and methods This prospective study enrolled 93 patients with pathologically diagnosed eCCA (54 males, 66.8 ± 9.0 years; 62 perihilar and 31 distal) and 43 patients without eCCA (19 males, 62.9 ± 11.8 years). All patients underwent conventional magnetic resonance imaging and OC-Z-DWI on an ultra-high gradient system (200 mT/m amplitude). Image quality of OC-Z-DWI was evaluated, and diagnostic performance and lesion sizing were compared between the conventional protocol and one incorporating OC-Z-DWI. Results OC-Z-DWI showed good scoring in noise, artifacts, and overall image quality (mean 3.83 ± 0.41, 3.65 ± 0.56, and 3.80 ± 0.43, respectively). Adding OC-Z-DWI to the conventional protocol significantly improved lesion edge sharpness (3.89 ± 0.31 vs 3.60 ± 0.53, P < 0.001), lesion conspicuity (3.94 ± 0.25 vs 3.75 ± 0.46, P < 0.001), diagnostic confidence (3.86 ± 0.38 vs 3.58 ± 0.65, P < 0.001), and diagnostic performance (AUC 0.917 vs 0.869, P = 0.018). Lesion size measurements with the OC-Z-DWI-based protocol demonstrated strong pathological correlation (r = 0.822), with lower pathological-imaging diameter discrepancy than the conventional protocol (median 4.0 mm vs 7.0 mm, P < 0.001). These improvements were consistent across both perihilar and distal subgroups. Furthermore, R0 resection patients exhibited a stronger imaging-pathology sizing correlation than R1 patients (r = 0.891 vs 0.528, P = 0.021). Conclusion Ultra-high gradient thin-slice OC-Z-DWI provides high-quality images for eCCA characterization. Adding OC-Z-DWI to the conventional magnetic resonance protocol enhances lesion delineation, diagnostic performance, and tumor sizing accuracy, delivering more precise preoperative information to optimize surgical planning.

title: Retrospective Lung-RADS v2022 Characterization of Fatal Lung Cancer Cases in the National Lung Screening Trial.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Persistent lung cancer mortality despite screening is multifactorial. Characterizing computed tomography (CT) findings preceding fatal lung cancer may identify imaging features and screening challenges that warrant further study. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective, outcome-enriched case series nested within the 26,722-participant low-dose computed tomography arm of the National Lung Screening Trial. Among 359 participants who died of lung cancer within the prespecified interval, exclusions for positive baseline screening (n = 186), incomplete screening (n = 28), withdrawal/declined screening (n = 19), unavailable CTs (n = 6), or three negative screens followed by death 2+ years after the final screen (n = 29) yielded 91 participants. Screening CTs were retrospectively assessed using the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) v2022. Four thoracic radiologists independently reviewed visible-in-retrospect nodules and adjudicated whether they met criteria for suspicion. Results Of 91 participants, 22 (24%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 17%-34%) had visible-in-retrospect nodules considered suspicious under Lung-RADS v2022 ("missed"), 16 (18%; 95% CI, 11%-27%) had visible nodules not meeting suspicion criteria ("not callable"), 50 (55%; 95% CI, 45%-65%) had no visible-in-retrospect nodule, and 3 (3.3%) were inconclusive. Missed nodules were frequently juxtapleural (41%), obscured (50%), or irregularly bordered (68%); not-callable nodules were frequently <6 mm (75%), juxtapleural (56%), or irregularly bordered (56%). Conclusion In this selected fatal-case series, small and juxtapleural nodules were common among visible nodules not meeting Lung-RADS v2022 suspicion criteria. These findings warrant evaluation in representative screening populations and should not be interpreted as estimates of population-level Lung-RADS performance.

title: Oral squamous cell carcinoma: A Modern Review of Pathogenesis and Treatment.
abstract: Oral cancer (OC), predominantly oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), is a serious global health burden with high mortality rates, especially in South and Southeast Asia. OC is a severe worldwide health issue that is mostly caused by a sedentary lifestyle, alcohol, tobacco, and areca nut intake. The highest prevalence of OSCC is in India and Southeast Asia. Complex genomic and epigenetic changes, such as TP53 dysfunction, enhanced EGFR alteration, and dysregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling pathways, in conjunction with tumor-promoting alterations in the tumor microenvironment, contribute to oral carcinogenesis ( Tan et al., 2023). Oral submucous fibrosis (a chronic condition that causes precancerous progression in mouth), and leukoplakia (white or grey patches to form on mucus membrane) are instances of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs), which are key indicators of cancer conversion. Even with advances in histopathology and imaging, delayed diagnosis remains a major limitation. Salivary biomarkers, liquid biopsy devices, and artificial intelligence-based screening tools are examples of novel diagnostic methods with potential for early diagnosis. Therapeutically, novel approaches such as immunotherapy, targeted therapy, nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems, electro spun nanofibers, and plant-derived phytoformulations offer innovative, multi-targeted strategies with enhanced efficacy and reduce toxicity. However, surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy continue to be the primary treatment approaches. Improving new interventions for OC treatment needs a multifaceted approach that integrates early detection strategies, advanced therapeutic strategies, the use of plant-derived therapeutics, nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and public health awareness to get better therapeutic outcomes.

title: A multimodal MRI radiomics sonata for differentiating small renal masses: a two-center retrospective study.
abstract: Background Accurately distinguishing benign from malignant small renal masses (SRMs) is crucial to avoid unnecessary surgeries, yet reliable preoperative diagnostic tools remain limited. Methods A total of 189 patients with SRMs from two hospitals (2018-2022) were enrolled. Clinical data and MRI features were analyzed by two radiologists. Radiomics features were automatically extracted from manually segmented ROIs using dedicated software. Significant features were selected via univariate analysis, multivariate regression, and Lasso to develop three models: radiomics, clinical, and combined nomogram. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC). Results The radiomics-clinical nomogram was constructed using T2WI signal intensity (p < 0.001), pseudocapsule (p = 0.001), and radiomics score (Rad-score, p = 0.001) via multivariate logistic regression. In the training set, the nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.962 (95% CI: 0.931-0.993), outperforming both the radiomics model (AUC = 0.918, 95% CI: 0.862-0.974) and the clinical model (AUC = 0.856, 95% CI: 0.780-0.933). Favorable performance was observed in the internal validation set (nomogram: AUC = 0.981, 95% CI: 0.944-1.000; radiomics model: AUC = 0.912, 95% CI: 0.750-1.000; clinical model: AUC = 0.844, 95% CI: 0.578-1.000) and external validation set (nomogram: AUC = 0.971, 95% CI: 0.886-1.000; radiomics model: AUC = 0.928, 95% CI: 0.841-0.989; clinical model: AUC = 0.916,95% CI: 0.760-0.976). Conclusion All three models enable effective and non-invasive preoperative differentiation of benign from malignant SRMs, with the radiomics-clinical nomogram exhibiting the highest diagnostic accuracy, supporting its potential as a valuable clinical tool.

title: Dual-state adaptive unrolled network for structure-preserving low-dose CT image restoration.
abstract: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but introduces spatially heterogeneous noise and artifacts that can obscure subtle anatomical structures. We address post-reconstruction image-domain LDCT restoration, where degradation suppression and structure preservation impose competing demands on a single restoration trajectory. We propose DSAUNet, a Dual-State Adaptive Unrolled Network that maintains persistent anatomy- and degradation-oriented latent states across unrolled stages. Rather than acting as transient feature branches, the evolving states participate in parameterizing subsequent restoration behavior through a degradation-oriented global policy coordinate for stage-level modulation and state-derived confidence variables for spatially selective regulation. Direction-aware prior modeling and multi-scale state guidance further realize this state-parameterized restoration process. Under the reported protocols, DSAUNet achieves 40.3721 dB PSNR and 0.9642 SSIM on 2DeteCT, exceeding the strongest baseline by 1.6320 dB and 0.0108, and achieves 47.4277 dB PSNR and 0.9846 SSIM under the patient-level five-fold Mayo evaluation, with a 1.0920 dB PSNR gain over the strongest PSNR baseline. On LoDoPaB-CT, it further obtains 38.5501 dB PSNR and 0.9141 SSIM, with the best PSNR, SSIM, and VIF among the compared methods. Controlled raw-state, persistent state-swapping, policy-coordinate, and confidence-map analyses support functionally differentiated state roles and active adaptive regulation. Bidirectional 2DeteCT-Mayo zero-shot experiments reveal direction-dependent transfer behavior, while unified profiling characterizes an accuracy-complexity trade-off. Together, these results support persistent dual-state controlled unrolling as a structured approach to image-domain LDCT restoration within the evaluated settings.

title: A robust biomarker combining radiomic and CA19.9 information to predict distant relapse-free survival after radiochemotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Background The radiomic feature Statistical Percentile 10% (p10%), extracted from [¹⁸F]FDG-PET images, has been previously identified and validated as a robust predictor of distant progression-free survival (DPFS) in unresectable pancreatic cancer (LAPC). This study aimed to maximize its prognostic potential by combining p10% with CA19.9 serum levels and assessing its generalizability across distinct clinical settings. Methods We analyzed 287 LAPC patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and a validation cohort of 72 patients enrolled in the CASSANDRA trial (resectable/borderline-resectable PDAC). Cox models combined p10% with CA19.9 levels measured before RT in LAPC patients, and before surgery for CASSANDRA patients. Results p10% was independently prognostic in both cohorts and its integration with CA19.9 significantly improved the prediction. In the LAPC cohort, the combined model achieved C-index=0.71, with median DPFS of 4.0-vs-15.0 months (p<0.0001;HR=3.22). In the pre-surgery setting (CASSANDRA trial), the model showed good rank-order discrimination (C-index=0.65), with median survival of 11.6 months vs not-reached (p=0.0018). However, the calibration slope of 0.54 suggests that absolute risk prediction requires recalibration in the surgical cohort. Conclusions Integrating p10% with CA19.9 provides a broader representation of tumor aggressiveness. The combined biomarkers demonstrate consistent performance across different disease stages supporting their use for treatment personalization.

title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Distal Aortopulmonary Window by Fetal Cardiac MRI.
abstract: Image Prenatal diagnosis of a distal aortopulmonary window by fetal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Case summary A fetus referred for cardiac MRI because of suboptimal visualization of the great vessels on ultrasound. MRI demonstrated a distal aortopulmonary window with a characteristic heart-shaped appearance of the great vessels. Take-home message Fetal cardiac MRI may provide complementary anatomical information when echocardiographic visualization is suboptimal and may help characterize complex fetal outflow tract abnormalities.

title: Cardiac CT Planning of Surgical Treatment of Multiple Coronary-Pulmonary Fistulas With Chronic Coronary Occlusion.
abstract: Anatomy Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies that may lead to myocardial ischemia through a coronary steal phenomenon, particularly when associated with coronary artery disease. Pathology We describe a case of cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) diagnosis of multiple coronary-pulmonary artery fistulas associated with chronic occlusion of the right coronary artery, in a 66-year-old man presenting with unstable angina. Imaging correlation CCTA and echocardiography were used for evaluation of procedural planning in an acute setting. Treatment The fistulas were effectively treated with surgical exclusion combined with coronary artery bypass grafting, yielding an optimal result on the postoperative computed tomography scan. Take-home messages Coronary fistulas are rare but important causes of myocardial ischemia. This case highlights the importance of CCTA definition of anatomical complexity and multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of complex coronary fistulas. Surgical repair remains the preferred approach in complex anatomy cases or associated coronary artery disease requiring revascularization.

title: Digitally Guided Root Membrane Preparation Using a Dedicated Apex Guide for Immediate Implant Placement: A Retrospective Case Series.
abstract: Objective To assess the clinical feasibility and 1-year outcomes of a static computer-assisted workflow using a dedicated Apex Guide for root membrane (RM) preparation and immediate implant placement. Methods Fifteen consecutive patients with nine anterior and six posterior single-tooth sites were included. Cone-beam computed tomography and intraoral scans were registered for planning. A tooth-supported Apex Guide guided a 2.0-mm drill along a root-oriented trajectory; implant placement used a separate prosthetically driven guide. Feasibility, complications, survival, Pink Esthetic Score (PES), probing depth (PD), bleeding on probing (BOP), recession and peri-implant marginal bone level (PIMBL) were assessed. Results Guided access and RM preparation were completed in all sites without intraoperative RM or facial bone damage. One RM became mobile and required removal; another developed internal exposure requiring reduction. RM retention was 93.3% (14/15), and implant and prosthetic survival were 100%. Between 6 months and 1 year, PES (12.13 ± 0.74 vs 12.20 ± 0.77; P = 0.317), PD (2.22 ± 0.15 vs 2.21 ± 0.10 mm; P = 0.655), BOP (3.34 ± 6.91% vs 2.23 ± 5.88%; P = 0.317) and PIMBL (0.280 ± 0.039 vs 0.281 ± 0.035 mm; P = 0.387) showed no significant changes. One screw loosening reduced prosthetic success to 93.3%. Conclusions The Apex Guide workflow was clinically feasible in this small series. RM-related complications occurred despite complete implant survival; comparative accuracy and long-term safety remain unestablished. Clinical relevance Static guidance may assist apical access during RM preparation while allowing independent, prosthetically driven implant placement.

title: Prospective Cardiac MRI study comparing Recovered COVID-19 patients with Recovered Non-COVID-19 Viral Respiratory Infection Patients (R-COVID-CMR).
abstract: Objective Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with subclinical myocardial inflammation. Post-COVID-19 infection, there are concerns about subsequent heart failure and persistent myocarditis. It is unknown how COVID-19 infection compares with non-COVID-19 viral infections in terms of myocardial inflammation based on cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) assessment. This prospective longitudinal study aims to determine and compare the extent and severity of myocardial involvement in patients with COVID-19 infection versus non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infections (control). Method Recruited recovered COVID-19 (RCOVID) patients and recovered non-COVID (non-COVID) patients from several hospitals and COVID-19-designated clinic underwent three CMR examinations for functional assessment, native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) quantification, with corroborating blood markers (NT-proBNP, white cell count, c-reactive protein, lactate dehydrogenase, and high sensitivity cardiac troponin T). CMR scans took place (i) within 2-week of confirmed recovery, (ii) 3-month, and (iii) 12-month post-recovery. Linear mixed model with Bonferroni correction was used for analysis. Results 152 participants were recruited, 112 RCOVID outpatients (mean age: 41.0; 58.9% female) and 40 non-COVID inpatients (mean age:45.0; 37.5% female). Non-COVID infections included influenza virus, rhinovirus/enterovirus, parainfluenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and human metapneumovirus. At all three time points, blood results and cardiac function parameters were not significantly different between RCOVID and non-COVID patient groups (p-value not significant). Both patient groups had no significant differences for native T1/T2 values, ECV, late gadolinium enhancement, T2 short tau inversion recovery, and overall fulfilment of the 2018 revised Lake Louise Criteria at each time points. Conclusion In this prospective longitudinal study with CMR examinations, COVID-19 infection does not cause a worse myocardial inflammatory response than non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infection in terms of CMR parameters, and blood markers. Plain english summary During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreaks, some COVID-19 patients were incidentally found to have inflammation of the muscular layer of the heart. Healthcare professionals were concerned the inflammation will lead to heart not delivering enough blood to meet body demands (ie. heart failure) in the long run. Therefore, we designed this study to better understand the extent and severity of cardiac involvement in patients with COVID-19 by comparing them to patients with other types of viral respiratory infections, such as influenza, which we were more familiar with. We recruited two groups of patients, one group with patients recovered from COVID-19, the other group with patients recovered from other types of viral respiratory infections. For each patient, we arranged three assessments at 2 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months after their recovery respectively. During each assessment, they had blood taken and underwent a cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) scan, a type of medical imaging used for assessment of heart function. 2018 revised Lake Louise Criteria (LLC) is a set of criteria for diagnosis of myocardial inflammation recommended by a group of experts. We compared the two groups of patients at each time point according to LLC, as well as their blood markers and heart function. In our study, we found that COVID-19 infection does not cause a worse heart muscle inflammatory response than other types of viral respiratory infections. This is reassuring as patients with previous COVID-19 infections will likely not develop inflammation of the heart muscle nor develop heart failure.

title: Basal forebrain glioma: Clinical characteristics and surgical treatment.
abstract: Background Surgical resection of basal forebrain (BFB) gliomas involving the anterior perforated substance (APS) is associated with a high risk of surgical complications due to multiple perforating arteries that traverse this region. Despite these challenges, surgery in this region serves several important purposes, including cytoreduction, histopathological diagnosis, and seizure control. Methods This study included a consecutive series of 67 patients with gliomas either confined to the BFB (13 cases) or extending to adjacent anatomical regions (54 cases) who underwent surgery at the Burdenko Neurosurgery Center between 2016 and 2023. Three main approaches were used: transsylvian, anterior interhemispheric, and supraorbital subfrontal. In 5 cases, the tumor was removed using a microsurgical burr-hole technique. Results BFB tumors were classified according to 2 features: 1) involvement of anatomical regions adjacent to the BFB and 2) localization of the tumor within the BFB: the septal region (S), anterior APS segment (Pa), and posterior APS segment (Pp). Isolated BFB tumors were found in 13 cases (19.4%), including 4 localized to the septal region. Among 59 patients with early postoperative MRI, median EOR was 82%. EOR 70-90% was achieved in 23 of 59 patients (39.0%), and EOR ≥ 90% in 25 of 59 (42.4%). With extension into the Pp segment, EOR ≥ 90% was achieved less often than in the remaining cohort: 8 of 31 (25.8%) versus 17 of 28 (60.7%), respectively (p = 0.009). Postoperatively, hemiparesis developed in 9 patients (13.4%) and speech disturbances in 12 (17.9%), most often because of injury to the lenticulostriate arteries. Hemiparesis resolved in 2 patients, whereas speech disturbances improved in 10 patients and persisted in 2 patients at 3-6 months. Complete seizure control was achieved in 31 of 44 patients (70.4%). Seizure control was better when EOR exceeded 70%. Multivariable Cox models including EOR and WHO grade showed no significant association between EOR and OS or PFS, whereas higher WHO grade was associated with worse OS and PFS. In the sensitivity analysis restricted to WHO grade 2-3 gliomas, greater EOR was associated with better OS (HR per 10% increase, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.29-0.99; p = 0.047), but not with PFS. Conclusions Resection of BFB gliomas is feasible with an acceptable risk of complications and provides effective seizure control. Greater EOR may be associated with better OS in WHO grade 2-3 gliomas. Tumor extension into the posterior portion of APS is associated with an increased risk of surgical morbidity during BFB glioma resection.

title: Digital Volumetric Planning and Mixed Reality-Guided Anterolateral Thigh Flap Reconstruction for Maxillary Defects.
abstract: Background Accurate restoration of soft-tissue volume remains challenging in maxillary reconstruction. This study assessed the feasibility of a defect-oriented digital volumetric planning workflow combined with mixed reality (MR)-guided anterolateral thigh flap (ALTF) harvest. Methods Patients who underwent maxillectomy followed by ALTF reconstruction between November 2023 and January 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Preoperative CT data were imported into Mimics Medical 21.0 for three-dimensional reconstruction of the maxilla and tumor. Virtual osteotomy and defect simulation were performed to calculate the simulated recipient-defect capacity, designated as V1. Flap dimensions were then designed using V1 and donor-site adipose thickness. MR guidance was used intraoperatively for perforator localization and flap harvest. Intraoperative flap volume was measured by water displacement (V2), and postoperative flap volume was quantified on CT imaging (V3). Secondary outcomes included flap utilization rate, complications, speech intelligibility, patient satisfaction, and University of Washington Quality of Life scores.The three related volumes were compared using the Friedman test, followed by Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Results Fifteen patients were included. Mean flap thickness was 10.80 ± 3.49 mm. Median V1, V2, and V3 values were 61.57 mL (interquartile range [IQR], 44.53), 75.00 mL (IQR, 52.00), and 64.26 mL (IQR, 40.65), respectively. The overall difference was significant (Friedman statistic = 17.200, degrees of freedom = 2; P < 0.001). V2 was significantly greater than V1 (adjusted P < 0.001) and V3 (adjusted P = 0.003), whereas V1 and V3 did not differ significantly (adjusted P = 1.000). Mean flap utilization rate was 91.13 ± 9.67%. All flaps survived. One patient developed titanium mesh exposure after radiotherapy; no other major complications occurred. Postoperative speech intelligibility and quality-of-life outcomes were generally favorable. Conclusions Digital volumetric planning combined with MR-guided ALTF harvest was technically feasible in this preliminary cohort and provided a reference for individualized flap design. The findings should be interpreted as exploratory, and comparative studies with larger samples are needed to determine whether this workflow improves clinical outcomes or reduces tissue trimming.

title: Prognostic factors in patients with lower gingival squamous cell carcinoma by computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging: an especial focus on mandibular canal invasion and masticator space invasion.
abstract: Introduction The study aimed to research the prognostic factors in patients with lower gingival squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) by computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), especially focus on mandibular canal invasion and masticator space invasion. Material & methods Forty-eight patients with lower gingival SCC underwent CT and MRI for pre-treatment. The prognostic factors were assessed by chi-square test with the Fisher's exact test. The five-year overall survival rates were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier method with log rank test. Results The results demonstrated that masticator space invasion with MRI was significant predictive variable for regional lymph node metastasis (p = 0.015), and that bone invasion with CT, masticator space invasion with MRI and T-primary tumour (TNM classification 9 th Edition) were significant predictive variables for survival (p < 0.001, p = 0.004 and p < 0.001, respectively). The five-year overall survival rate in bone invasion with CT was 77.1 % for non-mandibular canal invasion and 0 % for mandibular canal invasion, respectively (p < 0.001). The five-year overall survival rate in masticator space invasion with MRI was 68.8 % for no invasion and 12.5 % for masticator space invasion, respectively (p < 0.001). Furthermore, the five-year overall survival rate in T-primary tumour was 80.9 % for T1-3 and 7.1 % for T4, respectively (p < 0.001). Conclusion This study suggested that the mandibular canal invasion with CT may be a potential prognostic factor and that further multicenter validation is needed.

title: The medial collapse sign is associated with cubitus varus after pediatric supracondylar humeral fracture fixation: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Cubitus varus deformity is a common complication following pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures and rarely remodels spontaneously. However, surgeons lack a reliable intraoperative radiographic sign that directly reflects inadequate medial column reduction. This study aimed to evaluate whether the medial collapse sign (MCS) on immediate postoperative anteroposterior radiographs is associated with postoperative cubitus varus. Methods A retrospective cohort study included pediatric patients who underwent surgical treatment for supracondylar humeral fractures consecutively between January 2016 and March 2024. Fifty-two patients treated with reduction and cross pinning and followed for at least 6 months were included. Patients were categorized according to the presence or absence of cubitus varus at final follow-up (n = 20 and n = 32, respectively), which was radiographically defined as a side-to-side carrying-angle difference ≥5° on standing anteroposterior radiographs. Univariable and multivariable analyses were performed using Firth's penalized logistic regression. Results Presence of the MCS was strongly associated with cubitus varus (OR 155.4, 95% CI 24.8-1965.5; Holm-adjusted P < .001). MCS remained associated after adjustment for medial cortical comminution (OR 47.5, 95% CI 6.6-590.4, Holm-adjusted P < .001). The large effect size should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size. Sensitivity and specificity were 90.0% and 96.9%, respectively. Interobserver reliability was almost perfect (κ = 0.919). Conclusion The medial collapse sign is strongly associated with postoperative cubitus varus and may reflect inadequate medial column reduction. Recognition of the same medial cortical morphology on intraoperative fluoroscopy may prompt reassessment of alignment and reduction. Level of evidence Level III, Retrospective cohort comparison, prognosis study.

title: Optic disc drusen as a diagnostic confounder in a child with Alice in Wonderland syndrome.
abstract: We report the case of a 10-year-old boy referred for transient visual episodes compatible with Alice in Wonderland syndrome, described as a sensation that objects were moving away. Ophthalmic examination showed preserved visual acuity and an unremarkable anterior segment, but revealed elevation of the left optic disc, prompting evaluation for true papilledema. Macular OCT was normal, whereas optic nerve head OCT demonstrated structural asymmetry consistent with pseudopapilledema. Brain and orbital MRI showed isolated enlargement of both optic nerve sheaths and mild elevation of the left optic disc, without additional findings suggestive of intracranial hypertension. Orbital ultrasonography identified a hyperechogenic focus suggestive of optic disc drusen. The stable clinical and structural course supported the diagnosis of unilateral pseudopapilledema due to optic disc drusen, probably unrelated to the perceptual symptoms.

title: Post-registration medical imaging education as a pathway to addressing the specialist deficit in Rwanda: A needs assessment.
abstract: Introduction Sub-Saharan Africa faces a critical shortage of specialist medical imaging practitioners, yet undergraduate training remains insufficient for advanced practice. Rwanda's "4 × 4 Reform" prioritises expanding the radiology workforce, but evidence-based curriculum development for postgraduate education remains lacking. This study aimed to conduct a multi-stakeholder needs assessment to inform the design, structure, and delivery of a proposed Master of Science in Medical Imaging at the University of Rwanda, College of Medicine and Health Sciences. Methods An online cross-sectional survey was conducted nationally, recruiting 210 participants from multiple stakeholder groups, including clinical practitioners, educators, policymakers, and patient representatives. Data were analysed with descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact tests in R. Results Advanced image interpretation skills were identified as hugely lacking by 72.9% of respondents. Diagnostic ultrasound (68.8%), pattern recognition (65.2%), computed tomography (61.7%), and magnetic resonance imaging (60.7%) were the top priorities. Notably, 79.0% (n = 166) of stakeholders expected graduates to develop leadership and management skills, followed by teaching and curriculum development (73.8%). Fisher's exact tests comparing clinical practitioners (n = 142) with other stakeholders (n = 68) found no significant differences across all seven skills assessed (ultrasound: p = 0.2; pattern recognition: p = 0.2; CT: p = 0.4; MRI: p = 0.5; radiography: p > 0.9; nuclear medicine: p = 0.9; radiation therapy: p = 0.6). Conclusions This empirical assessment in Rwanda reveals an urgent need for specialist training that integrates advanced clinical competencies with leadership and education skills. Implications for practice This study offers a guide for integrating advanced clinical skills with leadership and educational competencies into postgraduate curricula, directly addressing critical workforce shortages in low-resource settings.

title: Advancing nanomaterials for treatment of eye diseases: a review.
abstract: Ocular diseases involving both the anterior and posterior segments-such as dry eye disease, keratitis, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion, and ocular tumors-remain major contributors to global visual impairment. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior-segment targets. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site-specific delivery. A wide range of engineered nanomaterials-including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid-based carriers, dendrimers, metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, cerium oxide nanozymes, carbon quantum dots, nanogels, and electrospun nanofibers-has demonstrated improved drug loading, sustained release, ocular surface retention, and compatibility with biologics and gene-based agents. Emerging minimally invasive platforms, such as 4D printed smart scaffolds, dissolving microneedles and magnetically driven microrobots, further enable precise transscleral or intravitreal delivery, active navigation through the vitreous, and targeted interaction with retinal lesions. Parallel clinical advances, including FDA-approved nanoformulations and ongoing trials, confirm the translational potential of these technologies. Plus, artificial intelligence now accelerates both ophthalmic diagnosis and nanocarrier design, enabling predictive modeling of nano-bio interactions, personalized delivery strategies, and real-time disease assessment. This review integrates current advances in nanomaterial engineering and AI-guided innovation, outlining their convergent roles in shaping next-generation precision therapeutics for vision preservation and restoration.

title: Impact of Photon-Counting CT Acquisition Modes on Coronary Stenosis Assessment and Radiation Dose: A Phantom and Clinical Evaluation.
abstract: Introduction Photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) offers high spatial resolution and dose-efficient coronary CT angiography (cCTA), but protocol selection, especially optimal acquisition mode, requires balancing spacial resolution, temporal robustness and radiation exposure. This study evaluated various PCD-CT acquisition modes in terms of image quality, blooming, stenosis grading, diagnostic accuracy, and radiation dose using phantom and clinical cCTA. Methods First-generation dual-source PCD-CT was used with four acquisition modes: high-pitch spiral with prospective ECG-gating (Flash), Sequence, Spiral, and retrospective ultra-high-resolution (UHR) spiral mode. Phantom experiments used six 3D-printed coronary artery models with stenoses ranging from 21% to 73%. In a retrospective clinical study, 41 cCTA examinations were analyzed. Qualitative and quantitative image assessments used invasive coronary angiography as reference standard for diagnostic accuracy. Patient characteristics and radiation doses were recorded. Results UHR demonstrated the highest image quality and the lowest quantitative blooming in phantom and clinical data (clinical image quality score: UHR 4.12 ± 0.99 vs. Flash 3.00 ± 0.86; p = 0.002). Diagnostic accuracy varied across protocols for detecting ≥50% and ≥70% stenoses was high across all modes (e.g., Flash: 76.5% each; Sequence: 100% and 57.1%; UHR: 64.7% and 82.4%). Radiation dose was highest in UHR (26.44 ± 9.76 mSv) compared with Sequence (13.65 ± 8.86 mSv) and Flash (1.40 ± 0.32 mSv); all p ≤ 0.011. Conclusion While UHR acquisition provides highest image quality in PCD-CT cCTA, lower-dose acquisition modes achieve comparable diagnostic accuracy for coronary stenosis detection. Protocol selection should therefore be individualized, and prospective controlled studies are required.

title: Uterine leiomyomas in HLRCC: a scoping review of presentation, histopathology, treatment patterns, and reproductive implications.
abstract: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC) is a rare cancer predisposition syndrome in which uterine leiomyomas (ULs) are common, morbid, and often precede renal cancer diagnosis. We synthetized evidence on the clinical presentation, pathology, management, and reproductive outcomes of HLRCC-associated ULs. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for peer-reviewed studies reporting original data on ULs in HLRCC. Two reviewers independently screened articles and extracted data. Individual patient data from 410 patients and aggregate data from 27 observational studies were included. Mean age at UL diagnosis was 32.4 years. Most patients (89.1%) had multiple fibroids, were symptomatic (88.1%), and commonly reported abnormal uterine bleeding (80.6%) or pelvic pain (41.2%). Average maximum fibroid size was 7.5 cm. Fumarate hydratase (FH) and/or S-(2-succino)cysteine (2SC) immunohistochemistry studies showed abnormal staining in >85% of tumors. Surgical intervention was required in 94.4% of patients; hysterectomy was most common (67.0%), at a mean age of 35.2 years, whereas myomectomy was performed in 27% at 27.7 years. Despite a family history of HLRCC-related features in 88.8% of patients, only 0.6% underwent germline FH testing before gynecologic diagnosis. Fertility and obstetric outcomes were sparsely reported. Uterine leiomyosarcoma was rare, with an uncertain syndromic association. HLRCC-associated ULs are genetically, morphologically, and clinically distinct from sporadic fibroids, yet remain under-recognized. Integrating age, multiplicity, symptoms, family history, and pathology-triggered FH/2SC immunohistochemistry into gynecologic practice would enable earlier germline testing, renal surveillance, and reproductive counseling. Prospective registries are needed to define genotype-phenotype relationships, fertility outcomes, and leiomyosarcoma risk.

title: The β-cells in type 1 diabetes mellitus: findings from human pancreas studies.
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by long-term and dynamic interactions between the immune system and pancreatic β-cells, ultimately leading to severe insulin deficiency. A paradigm shift in T1DM research has occurred in the past few years, with research now focusing on the human disease because of access to human pancreatic tissue and pancreas-draining lymph nodes. Advances in high-resolution imaging, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and histopathology based on artificial intelligence have profoundly reshaped our understanding of disease initiation and progression. These studies revealed that β-cell loss and/or dysfunction might begin earlier than previously appreciated, preferentially affecting small β-cell-rich islets and insulin-positive cell clusters, with larger islets showing transient resistance. Substantial β-cell mass often persists at diagnosis, accompanied by functional impairment rather than immediate cell death. Across disease stages, β-cells exhibit conserved molecular signatures dominated by interferon signalling, enhanced antigen presentation and adaptive immune-evasion programmes, with evidence of heterogeneity linked to age, disease duration and immune context. Parallel analyses of pancreatic lymph nodes show early immune dysregulation, including altered regulatory T cell signatures and expansion of stem-like cytotoxic T cell populations, even before overt hyperglycaemia. Together, these findings support an integrated model of T1DM progression that enables alignment of clinical staging with evolving β-cell and immune phenotypes.

title: Thermosensitive RGD-modified liposomes co-loading Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> and sorafenib for synergistic photothermal-chemotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Sorafenib (SRF) therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by dose-limiting toxicities, inadequate tumor exposure, and the inability to confine drug action spatiotemporally, leading to suboptimal efficacy and a narrow therapeutic window. Here we report an RGD-functionalized DPPC-based thermosensitive liposomal theranostic system co-encapsulating Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles and SRF (RGD-Fe 3 O 4 /SRF@TSL) to enable MRI-guided window selection and near-infrared (NIR)-triggered, on-demand chemotherapy potentiation. The nanosystem is colloidally stable (208 nm) and exhibits a phase transition at 41 °C. Accordingly, SRF release is sharply temperature-gated, reaching 88% at 45 °C but only 26% at 37 °C within 18 h (3.4-fold enhancement). Fe 3 O 4 confers strong T 2 MRI contrast ( r 2 = 136.4 mM -1 s -1 ) and photothermal conversion ( η = 24.73%), enabling noninvasive tracking of tumor accumulation and controllable local heating that elevates tumor-surface temperature to 56 °C within 5 min under 808 nm irradiation. Dynamic MRI identifies a pronounced tumor signal drop at ∼12 h post-injection, providing an imaging-defined irradiation window. RGD decoration improves cellular internalization (DiO-positive cells 80.6% vs . 55.8% at 3 h) and, together with NIR activation, increases ROS-associated signals, mitochondrial depolarization, and apoptosis (up to 46.4%) in vitro . In Hepa1-6 tumor-bearing mice, the image-guided combined regimen markedly suppresses tumor growth, reducing endpoint tumor weight from 1.1 g (PBS) to 0.1 g (91% reduction) without obvious acute toxicity under the tested conditions. This work establishes an operational "MRI-defined window → mild hyperthermia → thermosensitive release" paradigm to localize SRF action and improve the efficacy-toxicity balance for HCC therapy.

title: Clinical Spectrum and Insights from One Year of Ocular Genetics at a Single Tertiary Eye Care Centre.
abstract: Introduction Genetic testing benefits individuals and families with inherited eye diseases by facilitating accurate diagnosis, informing prognosis, enabling assessment for at-risk family members, and supporting targeted therapies. This study aimed to characterize the spectrum of inherited eye disorders and evaluate the diagnostic yield of genetic testing at a single tertiary eye care centre over a one-year period. Methods A retrospective review of patients attending the ocular genetics service at a tertiary eye care centre in India from January 1 to December 31, 2024, was conducted. Results Of 1325 patients evaluated, 862 (65%) underwent genetic testing. Inherited retinal disorders were the most common ( n = 440, 51%), followed by cornea and anterior segment disorders ( n = 107, 12.4%). Other conditions included hereditary optic nerve disorders ( n = 75, 8.7%), glaucoma ( n = 70, 8.1%), lenticular disorders ( n = 54, 6.3%), phacomatoses ( n = 25, 2.9%), ocular tumours ( n = 20, 2.3%), strabismus and albinism ( n = 19 and 18; ~2% each), MAC spectrum disorders ( n = 10, 1.4%), and systemic syndromes ( n = 22, 2.5%). Diagnostic yield was achieved in 605 (70%), while 257 (30%) remained inconclusive. Of the 463 untested families, the motivations were unascertained reasons ( n = 156, 33%), financial constraints ( n = 138, 30%), intent to test later ( n = 90, 19%), and belief that no treatment was available ( n = 79, 17%). Discussion Inherited retinal and anterior segment disorders constitute the most frequent genetic eye diseases. Genetic testing has enabled genotype-phenotype correlation in over two-thirds of cases. Financial constraints and limited availability of disease-modifying treatments remain key barriers for uptake of genetic testing.

title: Multimodal Imaging Characteristics of Sarcoid Retinal Granulomas.
abstract: Purpose To describe the clinical presentation and multimodal imaging characteristics of retinal granulomas in patients with ocular sarcoidosis. Methods In this retrospective observational case series, patients with definite or presumed ocular sarcoidosis presenting with retinal granulomas were evaluated. Multimodal retinal imaging was reviewed to characterize lesion morphology, imaging patterns, and longitudinal evolution. Results Retinal granulomas were identified in three patients with ocular sarcoidosis from diverse racial backgrounds. On fundus photographs, lesions ranged from multiple, superficial, small, faint yellow-gray nodules to more distinct, deeper yellow lesions, predominantly located in the mid- to peripheral retina. All retinal granulomas demonstrated hyperreflectivity on OCT with four distinct morphologic patterns: (1) inner and/or outer retinal granulomas; (2) retinal granulomas associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) disruption and hypertransmission defects; (3) sub-RPE granulomas located between the RPE and Bruch's membrane; and (4) combined chorioretinal granulomas extending from the choroid. FAF demonstrated predominantly isoautofluorescent lesions in the absence of RPE involvement, whereas hypoautofluorescence was observed when the RPE was involved. FA was available for one patient and demonstrated late hyperfluorescent staining of the retinal granulomas. Longitudinal imaging demonstrated evolution from active inflammatory nodules to regression with residual retinal and/or RPE changes, commonly manifesting as punched-out atrophic lesions. Conclusion Retinal granulomas may represent an underrecognized manifestation of ocular sarcoidosis. In our series, multimodal imaging allowed detailed characterization of their morphologic patterns and longitudinal evolution. Recognition of these characteristic imaging features of sarcoid retinal granulomas may facilitate consideration of sarcoidosis in the differential diagnosis of retinal infiltrative lesions.

title: High-fidelity 3D geometric reconstruction of pelvic organs from MRI: a hybrid deep learning and iterative optimization approach.
abstract: Objective The generation of high-fidelity, high-quality three-dimensional (3D) pelvic organ geometries from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived segmentation masks remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid framework for reconstructing the bladder, uterus, and rectum, and to assess its geometric fidelity, mesh-quality proxy performance, and reconstruction efficiency. Approach. We developed a hybrid deformable shape modeling framework that integrates deep learning prediction with iterative optimization for the reconstruction of the bladder, uterus, and rectum. The framework consists of three core components: (1) a geometry-aware multi-level deep learning architecture that preserves topological consistency of pelvic organs; (2) a two-stage amortized optimization training strategy that balances global shape capture and local surface refinement; and (3) a holistic synergy mechanism-where iterative optimization provides supervision for deep learning during the training phase, and during inference, deep learning rapidly predicts the global organ morphology, followed by iterative optimization to refine local surfaces and mesh quality. Main results. Before iterative refinement, the proposed model outperformed representative deep learning-based reconstruction methods in geometric fidelity, achieving CD/DSC values of 5.5 × 10⁻³/0.788 for the bladder, 3.7 × 10⁻³/0.839 for the rectum, and 4.2 × 10⁻³/0.900 for the uterus. Deep learning-based initialization enabled the complete hybrid framework to converge within approximately 100 iterations, with a reconstruction time of approximately 35 s per organ on a CPU and 1.5 s on a GPU. At the patient level, the mean minSICN and minSIGE values of the 10 worst volumetric elements were 0.0807 and 0.0844, respectively, exceeding those achieved by traditional geometric post-processing methods. Significance. The proposed framework connects image-domain segmentation with structural-domain applications by efficiently generating high-fidelity, high-quality pelvic organ geometries with improved mesh-quality proxy performance. These geometries may support statistical shape assessment and may provide candidate surface representations for subsequent volumetric meshing and solver-specific biomechanical validation.

The proposed framework connects image-domain segmentation with structural-domain applications by efficiently generating high-fidelity, high-quality pelvic organ geometries with improved mesh-quality proxy performance. These geometries may support statistical shape assessment and may provide candidate surface representations for subsequent volumetric meshing and solver-specific biomechanical validation.

title: Adaptive physics-inspired angular-spatial modeling for multi-shell diffusion MRI denoising.
abstract: Objective Multi-shell diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) provides rich q-space information but is susceptible to noise, which can disrupt spatial anatomy, intra-shell directional relationships, inter-shell signal attenuation, and downstream diffusion parameter estimation. We aim to develop a denoising method that jointly preserves spatial structure, directional information, and shell-specific signal characteristics. Approach We propose ASD-NCSM, an adaptive physics-inspired angular-spatial framework with a fixed three-stage alternating architecture. It combines intra-shell differential angular graph message passing with 2.5D spatial residual refinement. Noise-Conditioned Shell Modulation (NCSM) adaptively regulates angular updates according to b-value, spatial residual and angular dispersion proxies, and local gating. A Shell-wise Physical Attenuation and Angular Relation Consistency (SPARC) objective further constrains shell-wise signal fidelity, logarithmic attenuation, and local angular structure. The model was evaluated on HCP multi-shell dMRI with simulated noise and independently acquired real in vivo brain dMRI data. Main results Across five simulated noise levels from 2% to 10%, ASD-NCSM achieved the best overall DWI restoration among MPPCA, 1D-CNN, ECDM, SAN2N, and dMRI-Swin, with consistent subject-level advantages in PSNR, SSIM, and NRMSE. At 6% noise, principal-direction angular nRMSE was 32.68 ± 2.76%, with significant differences from all five baselines after Holm correction. ASD-NCSM also achieved the lowest mean MAE for FA, MD, AD, and RD, and the lowest relative MAE for ODI and FISO, while NDI was comparable to 1D-CNN and dMRI-Swin. For real data without noise-free references, Q-PEFT yielded the lowest angular cross-fit inconsistency (2.29 ± 0.10%) across three test subjects while maintaining limited signal and downstream-parameter changes. Significance ASD-NCSM jointly preserves spatial continuity, directional geometry, and shell-level attenuation, providing balanced signal recovery, directional preservation, and downstream parameter stability for multi-shell dMRI denoising.

title: Physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction for limited-angle CBCT.
abstract: Objective Limited-angle cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is attractive for imageguided radiotherapy and imaging-guided procedure when full-arc acquisition is impractical, but the incomplete angular sampling leads to severe streaking, shading, and structural distortion. This study aimed to develop a physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction framework for recovering anatomically faithful volumetric CBCT from limited-angle projections. Approach: We propose PCGA-Net, a dual-domain reconstruction framework that combines projection completion, analytic geometric reconstruction, and image-domain refinement within a unified cross-domain design. Specifically, a projection completion module first estimates missingangle information from the measured limited-angle projections. A geometry-aware reconstruction module then maps the completed projections into image space using differentiable cone-beam forward and backward-projection operators. Finally, a volumetric refinement module suppresses residual artifacts and restores anatomical detail under geometry-guided cross-domain consistency supervision. The framework was evaluated on three cohorts: gynecologic highdose-rate brachytherapy, abdominal liver 4DCT, and head-and-neck CBCT. Main Results: Across all three cohorts, PCGA-Net consistently outperformed conventional limitedangle FDK reconstruction and the compared learning-based baselines, cGAN and PatRecon-Net, in both qualitative and quantitative evaluation. On the gynecologic HDR brachytherapy cohort, PCGA-Net achieved an MAE of 34.47 ± 6.28 HU, an SSIM of 0.87 ± 0.04, and a PSNR of 35.79 ± 0.95 dB. On the abdominal liver 4DCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 39.27 ± 6.10 HU MAE, 0.82 ± 0.03 SSIM, and 36.85 ± 1.16 dB PSNR.On the head-and-neck CBCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 28.42 ± 4.88 HU MAE, 0.91 ± 0.05 SSIM, and 38.52 ± 0.95 dB PSNR. In all three cohorts, PCGA-Net exceeded cGAN and PatRecon-Net across all evaluated metrics. Significance: These results indicate that jointly enforcing projection-domain completion, analytic imaging geometry, and image-domain refinement is an effective strategy for limited-angle CBCT reconstruction. PCGA-Net provides a robust short-arc reconstruction framework across multiple anatomical sites, supporting its potential utility in constrained imageguided therapeutic and procedural settings.

title: Wavelet-based adaptive image fusion of CT and MRI with local neighborhood variance for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
abstract: Multimodal imaging of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) requires complementary representation of CT-derived bony anatomy and MRI-derived soft-tissue contrast. Existing fusion methods may fail to preserve both structural detail and soft-tissue information in a transparent and reproducible manner. We present a wavelet-based fusion framework that employs local neighborhood variance for adaptive weighting. This interpretable variance-driven strategy selectively integrates CT bony structures and MRI soft-tissue textures according to regional information content. The neighborhood configuration was selected through an ablation analysis of 232 clinical cases. Quantitative evaluation showed improved image-quality performance over the selected comparison methods across entropy, spatial frequency, average gradient, standard deviation, and edge information preservation factor, with respective gains of approximately 5.5%, 2.4%, 6.7%, 5.1%, and 3.2% relative to the best-performing baseline for each metric. These findings support the proposed method as an image fusion methodology for preserving complementary multimodal information; direct effects on target delineation, workflow efficiency, or dosimetric outcomes require future clinical validation.

title: Breast Implant Flipping: Prevalence, Clinical Correlation, and Independent Risk Factors in a Consecutive Ultrasound Cohort.
abstract: Background Silicone breast implants are designed with an anterior domed surface, and relatively flat posterior surface that contains the cured silicone patch. With implant flipping (an anterior-posterior malposition), the posterior patch rotates to an anterior position. Objectives There are currently no prospective published studies reporting the prevalence of implant flipping and its associated symptoms in aesthetic patients. This prospective study used in-office high-resolution ultrasound (HRUS) to evaluate the prevalence of breast implant flipping, assess associated changes in breast shape, appearance, and symptoms, and identify potential risk factors. Methods Consecutive patients with silicone breast implants presenting for routine follow-up underwent HRUS at 7 study sites in the United States over a 4-month period between April 1st and August 1st, 2026. Demographic data included age and BMI. Implant data included time since surgery, whether a primary of revision procedure, number of revisions, manufacturer, size, style, surface, use of ADM or scaffold, pocket location, capsule grade, flipped or not, and rupture. Results Five hundred and ninety consecutive patients were enrolled over 4 months. Mean age 43 years with range 22-82, mean BMI 23 with range of 16-34.5. Primary augmentations accounted for 64.6% of procedures, while revision augmentations accounted for 35.4%. Device manufacturer distribution, 63.9% Allergan, 12.4% Mentor, 15.9% Motiva, and 7.1% Sientra. Implant flipping was identified in 75 patients (12.7%). Conclusions Implant flipping was identified by HRUS in one in eight patients. Larger implant volume, prepectoral placement, and lack of soft tissue support were independently associated with flipping. HRUS improves detection, patient counseling, and surgical planning.

title: Modern Radiotherapy for Axial Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Impact of Gross Disease at Treatment Initiation.
abstract: To evaluate outcomes of modern radiotherapy (RT) for giant cell tumor of bone (GCTB) in anatomically constrained axial sites and to assess the prognostic impact of disease burden at RT initiation. We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed GCTB of the spine, sacrum, or skull treated with RT between 2006 and 2024 at a single institution. Patients treated with palliative intent and 1 patient lost to follow-up immediately after RT were excluded. Local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were calculated from RT initiation. Gross disease at RT was defined as a radiographically visible lesion on CT and/or MRI at RT initiation. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared by the log-rank test; prognostic factors were explored using univariate analyses. Seventeen patients were included (postoperative RT, n=13; salvage RT, n=3; definitive RT, n=1) and treated with 3D-conformal RT (n=9), IMRT (n=3), or proton therapy (n=5). Median follow-up was 79.8 months. The 5-year LRFS and PFS rates were 75.1% and 68.3%, respectively. Four patients experienced local recurrence and 1 developed lung metastasis. Gross disease at RT initiation (n=8) was significantly associated with inferior LRFS (5 y LRFS: 46.9% vs. 100.0% without gross disease; P=0.018). In this cohort of axial GCTB treated with modern RT, gross disease at RT initiation was associated with inferior local control. Outcomes appeared more favorable when RT was delivered in the absence of gross disease, suggesting that maximal safe debulking before RT may be relevant in selected anatomically constrained cases.

title: Anterior Segment Ischemia and Neurotrophic Keratopathy Following Ultrasound Cycloplasty in Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.
abstract: Ultrasound cycloplasty (UCP) is a minimally invasive, non-incisional glaucoma procedure that has emerged in recent years and is generally associated with few complications. We report a case of a patient with acute angle-closure glaucoma underwent UCP for IOP control. She developed iris neovascularization and neurotrophic keratopathy（NK）at postoperative week 6, followed by hypopyon, flattening of the anterior chamber, and thinning of the peripheral cornea at postoperative week 11, 12, and 14, respectively. We concluded that UCP can lead to anterior segment ischemia (ASI) and NK, which manifest as iris neovascularization, painless corneal epithelial defects, peripheral corneal thinning, hypopyon, and flattening of the anterior chamber. Preoperative screening for high-risk factors is essential before performing UCP.

title: In older adults, "mild" by GCS does not mean low risk: Multicenter study of 1,157 patients with mild TBI and acute subdural hematoma.
abstract: Background Acute traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) is the most common intracranial injury in mild TBI (mTBI), particularly in older adults. However, the relationship of patient and brain computed tomography (CT) characteristics with outcomes remains poorly described in a contemporary cohort. This study aims to characterize outcomes in younger and older adults with mTBI and isolated acute SDH. title: Noise2Match: Self-Supervised Low-Dose CT Denoising via Adaptive Inter-Slice Matching.
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, supervised convolutional neural network methods have greatly improved the performance of low-dose computed tomography (CT) denoising. However, they require paired noisy-clean training data, which is difficult to obtain in practice. Some classic self-supervised denoising methods rely on the assumption of pixel-wise independent noise, making them ineffective for correlated noise in low-dose CT (LDCT) images. Considering the high similarity and weaker noise correlation between adjacent CT slices, several recently proposed self-supervised methods use adjacent LDCT slices for training. Nevertheless, these approaches fail to effectively account for the non-rigid mis-alignment between slices caused by anatomical variation, hindering them from satisfying the equal-mean condition required by the classic Noise2Noise framework. In this paper, we propose Noise2Match, a self-supervised LDCT denoising method based on adaptive inter-slice matching. Noise2Match introduces an inter-slice matching network to model the label transition process between adjacent slices, and then applies correction to the denoiser's outputs to better satisfy the equal-mean condition. We theoretically prove that, under idealized conditions, training Noise2Match using adjacent LDCT slices is equivalent to supervised training with paired noisy-clean images. We further find that Noise2Match can also effectively perform low-dose cone-beam CT (CBCT) denoising, which could be attributed to its correction operation that reduces inter-slice noise correlation. To the best of our knowledge, Noise2Match is the first effective image-domain self-supervised method for low-dose CBCT. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Noise2Match outperforms existing image-domain self-supervised methods, offering broader applicability and higher practical value.

title: Integrating Plain 2D Ultrasound and Clinical Data for Identification of At-Risk MASH: A Multicenter Proof of Concept Study.
abstract: Background Identifying people with at-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a major challenge. We aimed to use deep learning to develop a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to facilitate the detection of at-risk MASH. Methods A multi-center cohort study was conducted across five tertiary hospitals in Japan and China. Clinical data and conventional ultrasound images were retrospectively collected. Organ segmentation using YOLO version 11 with quality control was performed, followed by creation of an EfficientNet-B6 CNN regression model, with image-level predictions averaged per patient, to estimate FAST and AGILE 3+ risk categories. Model performance was assessed using agreement across clinically relevant rule-out and rule-in thresholds, R 2 , root mean squared error (RMSE), and area under the receiver operating curve (AUROC). Results The final dataset comprised 416 patients for training (7643 images), 139 for internal validation (2463 images), and 154 for external testing (3539 images). The CNN model demonstrated good agreement with FAST (R 2 = 0.684; RMSE = 0.131; category agreement = 0.71) and moderate agreement with AGILE 3+ (R 2 = 0.445; RMSE = 0.1964; category agreement = 0.63). For FAST, AUROC was 0.974 (95% CI 0.947-0.993) for 0.35 and 0.932 (95% CI 0.884-0.969) for the 0.67 cut-off. For AGILE 3+, AUROC was 0.908 (95% CI 0.854-0.950) for 0.451 and 0.902 (95% CI 0.839-0.953) for the 0.679 cut-off. Conclusion The CNN model applied to clinical ultrasound images can approximate the accuracy of VCTE-based composite risk scores for detecting at-risk MASH. This may support the detection of at-risk MASH in settings with limited access to transient elastography.

title: Comparison Between Interlaminar and Transforaminal Endoscopic Lumbar Discectomy for Sciatic Scoliosis Secondary to Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Study With a Minimum 1 Year Follow-Up.
abstract: Objective This study aims to compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of interlaminar and transforaminal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (IELD and TELD) in the treatment of lumbar disc herniation (LDH) with sciatic scoliosis. Methods Patients with sciatic scoliosis secondary to LDH who had undergone IELD or TELD between January 2022 to June 2024 were reviewed. Radiographic parameters, including Cobb angle, apical vertebral translation (AVT), and coronal balance distance (CBD), were measured preoperatively and postoperatively to assess curve evolution. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Meanwhile, perioperative data were also collected. Comparisons between the groups were made by independent t-tests and χ 2 tests. Results A total of 134 patients in the IELD group and 103 patients in the TELD group were included in this study. There was no significant difference in intraoperative blood loss (13.4 ± 7.8 mL vs. 11.5 ± 7.1 mL, p = 0.067) and postoperative length of stay (2.5 ± 0.6 days vs. 2.5 ± 0.8 days, p = 0.378) between the two groups; however, the IELD group demonstrated shorter operation time (87.2 ± 17.4 min vs. 96.1 ± 23.3 min, p = 0.001) and fewer intraoperative fluoroscopy times (4.9 ± 0.7 vs. 10.3 ± 2.7, p < 0.001) compared to the TELD group. Both groups showed significant improvements in VAS and ODI scores (p < 0.05), with no significant differences between the groups. Before surgery, 86.9% (206/237) patients had a disc herniation at the convex side of the lumbosacral curve and 86.5% (205/237) patients showed a trunk shift toward the opposite side of disc herniation. After surgery, 91.8% (123/134) of the IELD group and 90.3% (93/103) of the TELD group achieved resolution of scoliosis (AVT ≤ 10 mm) within 12 months. At the final follow-up, the AVT, Cobb angle, CBD, and SVA in the IELD group were 2.7 ± 2.0 mm, 1.0° ± 0.8°, 1.2 ± 0.9 mm, and 3.4 ± 3.1 mm, respectively, with no significant differences compared to the 2.8 ± 2.7 mm, 1.1° ± 0.8°, 1.2 ± 0.8 mm, and 3.7 ± 3.5 mm in the TELD group. Conclusions Both IELD and TELD are effective and safe for LDH with sciatic scoliosis, with comparable radiographic and clinical outcomes in terms of scoliosis correction. IELD is associated with shorter operation time and fewer intraoperative fluoroscopy times in this cohort.

title: Amyloid-β Immunotherapy in Alzheimer's Disease: Challenges and Opportunities.
abstract: Passive anti-amyloid-β immunotherapy has shifted from repeated phase 3 failure to reproducible, although modest, clinical slowing in biomarker-defined early Alzheimer's disease. We review lessons from first-generation antibodies, including inadequate target engagement, late-stage enrollment, and limited outcome sensitivity. We then compare second-generation agents (i.e., aducanumab, lecanemab, and donanemab) highlighting amyloid-β species selectivity, plaque clearance kinetics, and durability, and we discuss emerging delivery innovations. Safety is dominated by amyloid-related imaging abnormalities, likely reflecting cerebrovascular amyloid vulnerability, and requires timely baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) screening; APOE -informed counseling; and standardized, front-loaded MRI surveillance with symptom-triggered evaluation. We summarize prevention trials in autosomal dominant and sporadic preclinical populations and consider prospects for combination or sequential regimens with tau-targeting therapies. Finally, we focus on biomarker-guided implementation: blood-based prescreening, confirmation pathways, monitoring of biological response, and treat-to-clear or stopping concepts, alongside unresolved issues of health-system readiness, equity, and budget impact. Registry-enabled learning is emphasized to generate real-world safety and effectiveness evidence.

title: Next-Generation Sequencing to Identify Genetic Causes of Chinese Patients Affected With Non-retinal Developmental Eye Disorders.
abstract: To investigate the genetic causes of non-retinal developmental eye disorders in 14 Chinese different families, we subjected participants to a specific hereditary eye disease enrichment panel (HEDEP) or whole exome sequencing. We further validated disease-causing variants and performed co-segregation analyses on the available family members by Sanger sequencing. We classified sequence changes according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology variant interpretation guidelines. Fourteen probands with diverse clinical diagnoses were analyzed, including microphthalmia (with or without microcornea and congenital cataract or congenital corneal opacification (CCO), four cases), anterior segment dysgenesis (ASD, six cases)-including Peter's anomaly (PA, one case), PA and microphthalmia (one case), iridocoloboma or aniridia (with microcornea and/or congenital cataract, two cases), and primary congenital glaucoma (PCG, two cases)-congenital cataract (with CCO or microcornea, three cases), and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS, one case). Initial inheritance patterns for 1, 5, and 8 cases were autosomal recessive, autosomal dominant, and sporadic, respectively. We identified 17 (likely) pathogenic variants and one variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in 16 genes, including BMP4, BCOR, PITX3, and PAX6. Among them, eight were novel variants, and two were de novo. We confirmed the pathogenicity of PAX6 intronic mutation using in vitro splice assays and redefined the pathogenicity of the variants of uncertain significance as likely pathogenic. Patients with developmental eye diseases typically have complex ocular and systemic phenotypes, possibly leading to significant visual impairment and high blindness rates. Identifying the genetic causes facilitates early diagnosis and effective treatment and rehabilitation strategies, thereby providing valuable insights for genetic and clinical counseling of these patients.

We identified 17 (likely) pathogenic variants and one variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in 16 genes, including BMP4, BCOR, PITX3, and PAX6. Among them, eight were novel variants, and two were de novo. We confirmed the pathogenicity of PAX6 intronic mutation using in vitro splice assays and redefined the pathogenicity of the variants of uncertain significance as likely pathogenic. Patients with developmental eye diseases typically have complex ocular and systemic phenotypes, possibly leading to significant visual impairment and high blindness rates. Identifying the genetic causes facilitates early diagnosis and effective treatment and rehabilitation strategies, thereby providing valuable insights for genetic and clinical counseling of these patients.

title: Guidelines for Colonic Diverticular Disease-2026, Second Edition: Management of Diverticular Bleeding and Acute Diverticulitis.
abstract: Colonic diverticular disease is becoming increasingly common in Japan, paralleling population aging and changes in lifestyle and medication use. The predominance of right-sided diverticulosis in Asian populations, in contrast to the left-sided predominance in Western populations, influences clinical presentation and management. In Japan, diverticulitis has become a clinically important problem, and diverticular bleeding is currently the most frequent cause of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB). The Japanese Gastroenterological Association updated its clinical guidelines for diverticular bleeding and diverticulitis in 2026. Key domains including epidemiology, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and priority clinical and future research questions were addressed. Evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, and recommendations were formulated via a modified Delphi process with external review. These guidelines aim to provide Japanese and Asian evidence-based consensus that complements Western guidelines. Recommendations for acute LGIB and diverticular bleeding are as follows: risk stratification with the Shock Index and Oakland and NOBLADS scores guides triage; pre-colonoscopy contrast-enhanced computed tomography is the widely used diagnostic modality; routine colonoscopy within 24 h is not suggested for all patients; endoscopic band ligation or direct clipping is suggested post-detection of stigmata of recent hemorrhage; and early oral refeeding is suggested. Recommendations for diverticulitis are as follows: post-resolution colonoscopy is suggested to exclude colorectal cancer; outpatient treatment and withholding of antibiotics are suggested in selected uncomplicated cases; and primary anastomosis may be favored over Hartmann's procedure in selected complicated cases.

title: Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
abstract: Background Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information. Methods In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed. Results Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P <0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis. Conclusions Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in patients undergoing coronary CT angiography. Circulating TMAO provides complementary prognostic information and refines risk stratification, particularly among individuals without functionally significant ischemia. Integrating systemic biomarkers with coronary physiological assessment may improve individualized risk evaluation beyond imaging alone.

title: Sex differences and prevalence of prior deep vein thrombosis among patients with incidental iliac vein compression on computed tomography.
abstract: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify risk factors and evaluate clinical outcomes associated with incidental left common iliac vein compression on CT imaging.MethodsThis is a retrospective study that reviewed venous-phase abdomen and pelvis CT scans to identify patients with incidental extrinsic compression of the left common iliac vein due to an overlying right common iliac artery. A total of 726 patients were included (364 females, 362 males; mean patient age: 61.9 ± 15.9 years). Board-certified radiologists reviewed all CT scans. Significant left iliac vein compression was defined as >50% luminal narrowing.ResultsSignificant iliac vein compression was identified in 114 (15.7%) patients and was more common in females (19.5%) versus males (11.9%) ( p < 0.01). Patients with iliac vein compression >50% had significantly lower BMI than those without compression (24.8 ± 6.2 vs 28.7 ± 7.2 kg/m 2 , p < 0.01). Patients with incidental left iliac vein compression had a higher rate of prior left lower extremity DVT ( p = 0.02).ConclusionIncidental left common iliac vein compression was present in approximately 16% of patients and was more frequent among females. Compression was associated with lower BMI and more than twice the rate of ipsilateral DVT, despite no prior diagnosis of MTS. These findings suggest that incidental iliac vein compression could have more clinical significance than previously recognized.
